title: DDCL-GAN: a novel dual-domain contrastive learning generative adversarial network for unsupervised multimodal remote sensing image change detection
abstract: Change detection (CD), as a core task in remote sensing image analysis, plays a crucial role in disaster monitoring, urban planning, and environmental assessment. Compared to traditional CD methods, multimodal CD breaks the dependency limitations on homogeneous sensor data, demonstrating higher timeliness and flexibility in disaster emergency response. However, significant imaging differences between different sensors lead to a lack of comparability in multimodal images, severely hindering their practical application. Existing multimodal CD research has effectively alleviated this issue by introducing generative adversarial networks (GANs) to transform multimodal images into the same image domain. Nevertheless, these methods generally overlook the negative impact of intrinsic change regions on image transformation quality and the enhancement of CD performance through complementary features between different modalities, resulting in limited change recognition accuracy. To address these shortcomings, we propose a novel dual-domain contrastive learning GAN (DDCL-GAN) for unsupervised multimodal CD. This network effectively suppresses interference from change regions through a carefully designed non-local spatial correlation patch contrastive learning strategy, thereby ensuring semantic consistency at the content level between transformed and original images. Additionally, we develop a multi-scale dual residual module and a semantic cross-flow alignment module to enhance the model’s ability to express multi-scale semantic information and fine-grained features, respectively. Finally, we construct a dual-domain difference markov random field (DDMRF) detection model, which effectively improves detection performance by simultaneously considering dual-domain image information. To validate the effectiveness of the proposed method, we conducted comparative experiments with twelve mainstream unsupervised multimodal CD methods on nine typical datasets. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves optimal performance across multiple average quantitative metrics, particularly in terms of mean IoU and κ, showing improvements of at least 2.9% and 2.3%, respectively, compared to comparative methods.

title: APGFusion : Adaptive PoolFormer and CNN medical image fusion network based on convolutional gated linear units
abstract: Medical image fusion combines important information from images taken by different sensors into one image. This process produces clearer fused images and eliminates unnecessary details, thereby enhancing the efficiency of clinical analysis and improving diagnostic accuracy. However, existing multimodal medical image fusion models often lose global and local features when handling complex fusion strategies and fail to ensure visual naturalness in the fused results. Moreover, most current models lack sufficient exploration of multi-channel data, reducing the clinical reliability of fusion outcomes. To solve these issues, we designed a novel deep model named APGFusion. The model uses an adaptive dual-branch network that effectively fuses global and local features with high quality. First, we apply the adaptive feature fusion (AFF) module in the field of medical image fusion for the first time. This module effectively extracts local features and global representations, resulting in a richer semantic representation of the fused images. Second, we propose a TransGLU module that combines the convolutional gated linear units module from TransNeXt for shared feature extraction and reconstruction, implementing an attention mechanism for channel mixing to selectively choose important features and dynamically adjust the feature fusion strategy. TransGLU allows for diverse medical image characteristics and outcomes, addressing the limitations of traditional medical image fusion methods in information integration and feature extraction.The proposed model adaptively adjusts feature weights across modalities, ensuring superior visual and structural fusion performance. Our proposed model demonstrated significant improvements on the Harvard dataset. title: Navigating multi-source threats in low-altitude urban airspace: A physics-informed cyclotron meta-heuristic method
abstract: The emergence of the low-altitude economy has led to increasingly dense electromagnetic (EM) and radar coverage, complex morphology, and dynamic weather in urban airspace. This complex environment renders the task for UAVs to navigate (also known as trajectory planning) a highly nonlinear and multi-constrained global optimization problem under multi-source dynamic threats. A physics-inspired Cyclotron Accelerator Optimization Framework (CAOF) is proposed, in which magnetic-field deflection promotes global exploration, electric-field acceleration enhances local exploitation, and rhythmic scheduling achieves dynamic balance. Instantiating CAOF with the Grey Wolf Optimizer as the foundational algorithm yields CA-GWO, an approach with controllable exploration capacity and robust convergence. To faithfully approximate urban low-altitude conditions, DEM/OSM data, base-station and radar layouts, historical meteorology, and wind fields are integrated into a high-fidelity cost model that accounts for energy consumption, Electromagnetic and radar exposure, path smoothness, and occlusion. Experimental results across single-route, deep-penetration, and closed-loop scenarios demonstrate that CA-GWO generates stable trajectories. Compared to four state-of-the-art planners, it achieves significant improvements in fitness and path compactness, while simultaneously reducing electromagnetic and radar exposure and maintaining stable altitude.

title: Multi-perspective prompt and assimilated self-modulation transformer for adverse weather removal
abstract: Existing methods for adverse weather removal struggle to learn consistent cross-degradation patterns and lack a robust prompt strategy, leading to sub-optimal all-in-one image restoration performance. To this end, we introduce a novel Multi-perspective prompt and Assimilated self-modulation Transformer for All-in-one Image Restoration, denoted as MATAIR. Our approach first examines the uniformity of features across different degradations in the spatial domain, and introduces an assimilated self-modulation attention (AMA) mechanism, which achieves the distribution alignment of various degradations and avoids the excessive reliance on specific feature structures. Additionally, we propose a multi-perspective disentangling prompt (MDP) strategy, which utilizes the prompts from multiple views to prompt the disentangling features and overcomes the representation limitations of existing single-view prompt methods. Extensive experiments on eight public datasets demonstrate that our proposed approach outperforms the recent state-of-the-art methods in both the image quality and inference time.

title: Dual-channel attention-autoencoder for tabular-graph fusion: tackling heterogeneous data in AI for Science
abstract: Integrating mainstream heterogeneous data, specifically structured tabular data and microscopic graph structure data, remains a critical challenge in the field of AI for Science. This study introduces a multimodal co-optimization model based on attention mechanism and auto-encoder (MMAE), which employs a dual-channel architecture to process experimental data in tabular form and microscopic structural data in graph form. A dynamically weighted attention mechanism enhances data modeling capabilities. Furthermore, addressing the lack of effective deep learning baselines for structured tabular data, this research proposes a deep learning tabular task model based on weighted learning strategy and attention mechanism (WLTAB), which supports cross-modal collaborative optimization. To validate the model’s efficacy, experiments were conducted using the OSN and NF membrane separation datasets. Results indicate that the MMAE model significantly outperforms existing multimodal fusion and single-modal modeling methods. It not only enhances the accuracy and depth of multi-modal fusion but also effectively mitigates issues of information distortion and modal inconsistency. Additionally, the multi-modal model was optimized and enhanced using variational quantum circuits (VQC), leading to an approximate 80% reduction in parameters and a substantial decrease in model optimization complexity. By addressing the challenge of heterogeneous data representation in scientific domains and achieving efficient cross-modal fusion, this study offers a transferable multi-modal methodological framework for AI for Science.

title: PrivTSAD-FedWGAN: A novel federated learning and WGAN framework for privacy-preserving multivariate time series anomaly detection
abstract: The growing reliance on cloud data centers for large-scale data analysis, particularly in sensitive domains like healthcare and finance, raises critical privacy concerns when sharing raw information. Existing anomaly detection methods often overlook privacy-preserving mechanisms, leaving sensitive data vulnerable during collaborative analysis. To bridge this gap, we propose PrivTSAD-FedWGAN, an unsupervised framework combining federated learning with a gradient-penalized Wasserstein Generative Adversarial Network (WGAN-GP) for privacy-aware anomaly detection in multivariate time series. PrivTSAD-FedWGAN decentralizes model training to local clients, thus avoiding raw data exchange. The integration of WGAN-GP mitigates mode collapse and stabilizes training using Wasserstein distance and gradient penalty. We introduce a composite anomaly score, unifying reconstruction, discrimination, and prediction errors to improve detection accuracy while preserving temporal dependencies. Extensive experiments on four comprehensive datasets (PSM, SMAP, MSL, SMD) show that, under federated learning, PrivTSAD-FedWGAN achieves F1 scores of 96.49%, 81.93%, and 91.53%, outperforming the next-best methods by 9.85, 28.27, and 17.6 percentage points, respectively. Even in centralized settings, it surpasses existing methods, improving F1 scores by 3.07 (PSM) and 4.75 (MSL) percentage points and demonstrates superior performance, establishing a new state-of-the-art. These results demonstrate the framework’s effectiveness in balancing privacy preservation with high detection performance, addressing the need for secure anomaly analysis in distributed environments.

title: An empirical analysis of deep learning methods for small object detection from satellite imagery
abstract: Despite a substantial body of literature on object detection, there is a notable lack of empirical studies on detecting small objects. Additionally, the definition of a small object remains unclear. This paper presents a thorough evaluation of six state-of-the-art deep learning methods for small object detection from satellite imagery. Three public high-resolution datasets are used to understand various influential aspects and the generalization ability. Among the six methods, YOLOv11 achieves a balanced performance for localization and adaptability, while Faster R-CNN maintains consistent detection coverage. Anchor box-based methods require extensive fine-tuning, whereas transformer-based methods demand greater computational resources to achieve competitive results. In addition, anchor-based methods, including SSD, Faster R-CNN, and Cascade R-CNN, are sensitive to the anchor box size, and, for small object detection, a small to moderate size is preferred. Both deformable and RT-DETR methods are susceptible to overfitting. RT-DETR exhibits superior detection in partial occlusion scenarios, particularly through vegetation and shadows, whereas deformable DETR struggles to identify individual small objects in dense clusters. Comparing computational efficiency with a batch size of one reveals that RT-DETR and YOLOv11 are more training-intensive, with optimizations focused on inference. Methods such as Faster R-CNN have a larger memory footprint but lower computational costs and time requirements.

title: MCPT-CAF-BiGRU: A multi-scale CNN and ProbSparse-Masked Transformer model with cross-attention fusion and BiGRU for hourly wind speed forecasting
abstract:
Wind speed forecasting is essential for reliable wind power integration but remains challenging due to the inherent non-stationarity, multi-scale variability, and spatial heterogeneity of wind fields. To address these issues, we propose MCPT-CAF-BiGRU, a hybrid deep learning framework that combines Multi-scale Convolutional Neural Networks (MCNN), ProbSparse-Masked Transformer, Bidirectional Gated Recurrent Unit (BiGRU), and a Cross-Attention Fusion (CAF) mechanism. The MCNN captures local disturbances across multiple temporal scales, while the ProbSparse-Transformer efficiently models long-range dependencies, and BiGRU further enhances bidirectional contextual representation. The CAF mechanism adaptively integrates local and global feature streams, improving robustness under turbulent dynamics.

Extensive experiments on four real-world wind farm datasets at three heights (10, 30, and 50 m) show that MCPT-CAF-BiGRU consistently outperforms eleven benchmark models in terms of RMSE, MAE, MAPE, and NSC, demonstrating superior accuracy and generalization across diverse wind regimes. Ablation studies confirm the contribution of each architectural component. These findings establish MCPT-CAF-BiGRU as an effective solution for multi-altitude wind speed forecasting, providing methodological innovation and practical support for intelligent wind energy scheduling.

title: KA-DDI: A knowledge-adaptive contrastive learning framework for drug-drug interaction prediction
abstract: Accurate prediction of drug-drug interactions (DDIs) is imperative for ensuring drug safety. While methods leveraging knowledge graphs (KGs) have demonstrated potential, they are confronted with two fundamental challenges: knowledge overload, where noisy connections in biomedical KGs obfuscate critical information, and interaction dominance, where models overfit observed DDI links, disregarding more comprehensive semantic knowledge. To overcome these challenges, we propose KA-DDI, a novel knowledge-adaptive contrastive learning framework. Its core innovation is a relation-aware sampling strategy within a dual-graph adaptive contrastive learning module. This strategy dynamically refines the graph structures to suppress task-irrelevant connections and emphasize pharmacologically relevant relations. KA-DDI first integrates drug molecular structures and sequences via a multi-modal fusion module. The refined graphs are then encoded by view-specific networks and aligned via contrastive learning. Additionally, the multi-task learning framework enhances the model by incorporating multiple objectives, combining DDI prediction with knowledge graph regularization and contrastive alignment tasks to prevent overfitting and ensure generalization. Extensive experiments on DrugBank and KEGG datasets demonstrate that KA-DDI significantly outperforms state-of-the-art baselines. The results confirm that our framework effectively mitigates knowledge overload and interaction dominance, leading to more robust and accurate DDI predictions.

title: MPRL: Multi-perspective representation learning for accurate and generalizable protein solubility prediction
abstract: Heterologous expression of recombinant proteins is a critical approach in protein production and manufacturing. However, it often exhibits low solubility in host cells, which limits its scalability in modern industrial applications. Protein solubility not only significantly affects biological activity but also plays a vital role in disease understanding and drug development. Therefore, establishing efficient computational methods for solubility prediction holds significant importance for biomanufacturing. Traditional prediction approaches, which primarily rely on physical simulations and simple machine learning techniques, are often constrained by computational cost and dataset size, making them inadequate for handling the complexity and diversity of modern scenarios. With the advancement of deep learning, numerous computational methods have emerged, achieving remarkable results. Nevertheless, these approaches often lack a unified and comprehensive learning framework for mining protein sequence information, which results in learning biases that limit their generalization ability. To address these issues, this study proposes a multi-level protein feature extraction framework from four distinct perspectives: implicit evolutionary information, local regions, sequence patterns, and global potential interactions. Our method aims to capture key semantic information and improve the accuracy of protein solubility prediction. The proposed method is trained on the newest Escherichia coli dataset and evaluated on both an independent test set and an external wet-lab dataset. The results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms state-of-the-art approaches and exhibits strong generalization capabilities.

title: X-CLPA: A contrastive learning and prototypical alignment-based crossmodal remote sensing image retrieval
abstract: Information retrieval across modalities has become crucial in remote sensing (RS) with ever-growing multimodal satellite data and the requirement of multiple perspectives in RS scene analysis. These techniques are often helpful in disaster management and land use mapping as they can retrieve information from different time periods and geographical locations. However, crossmodal image retrieval comes with its own set of challenges like variation in statistical properties and heterogeneity gap. This paper proposes a novel crossmodal image retrieval algorithm based on contrastive learning and prototypical alignment (X-CLPA) which aims to overcome the above challenges and is capable of retrieving images from multiple modalities like optical, multispectral (MS), synthetic aperture radar (SAR), and panchromatic (PAN). The backbone network is a hybrid ResNet module that can capture salient features, and an attention based context-aware pooling is performed to identify interpixel relationships. A novel combination of objective functions – the crossmodal contrastive loss which helps to distinctively identify classes across modalities, and the crossmodal prototype alignment loss which aligns the modalities in a common feature space – is used. The algorithm is tested on EuroSAT, DSRSID and TUM datasets, and the model is able to achieve 98.69% mAP in the DSRSID dataset, 95.96% in EuroSAT dataset (RGB, MS), and 99.31% in TUM dataset. Extensive experiments were conducted to further test the efficacy of the model, and the results show that X-CLPA exhibits superior overall performance.

title: SeisMind: A domain-knowledge-informed reinforcement learning framework for intelligent control of structural seismic response
abstract: Active and intelligent control of structural seismic response has become a key approach for enhancing the safety and resilience of civil infrastructure. However, traditional model-based active controllers typically rely on accurate structural models and fixed control laws, which may perform poorly under complex real-world conditions. To address these limitations, this study proposes SeisMind, an end-to-end seismic control framework in which control policies are optimized using deep reinforcement learning. To handle unpredictable seismic excitations, a stochastic training environment is established by systematically sampling a wide range of near-field and far-field earthquake records, capturing diverse frequency contents, intensity levels, and seismic characteristics. To improve the robustness of the control strategy, structural uncertainties, particularly stiffness degradation, are incorporated via domain randomization during training. In addition, a physically interpretable reward function is designed to integrate structural response indicators capturing both structural and non-structural damage, as well as actuator effort. Numerical experiments demonstrate that SeisMind achieves effective control performance across linear and nonlinear structural systems, maintaining stable performance even under structural degradation. Across multiple seismic intensity levels, SeisMind exhibits more stable, self-adaptive, and less variable control performance across a range of ground motion records, outperforming conventional Linear Quadratic Regulator and H_{∞} robust controllers, thereby highlighting its potential as a scalable and generalizable solution for next-generation intelligent seismic control of civil infrastructure.

title: DualBind: Dual-module protein-ligand binding affinity prediction with adaptive GNN and structure-aware transformer
abstract: Protein-ligand binding affinity (PLA) prediction plays a pivotal role in drug discovery. Although previous in-silico approaches have presented promising performance, they predominantly focus on a single perspective, often failing to simultaneously capture the intricate mutual effects among molecules and the distinct mechanisms of action inherent within these complexes. In this study, we propose DualBind, a novel dual-module framework that integrates the strengths of both interaction-free and interaction-based paradigms. DualBind simultaneously models individual characteristics of ligands, pockets, and proteins, as well as their mutual effects. Specifically, the interaction-free module employs a Structure-aware Transformer to capture both local and global relationships among molecules. Meanwhile, the interaction-based module leverages an adaptive graph neural network to model intra- and inter-molecular interactions. This dual-module architecture facilitates the extraction of both coarse sequence-level and fine-grained graph-level features, enhancing representation learning and PLA prediction accuracy. Comprehensive experiments on three datasets demonstrated that DualBind consistently outperformed state-of-the-art methods, achieving a 4.3% reduction in RMSE, while visualization tests on HDAC families further confirmed its biological relevance and reliability. The code is available at https://github.com/Arirhenium/DualBind.

title: Generative AI in different imaging modalities for disease diagnosis: A review
abstract: The rapid development of Artificial Intelligence (AI) has led to significant advances in several industries, particularly in medical imaging. Notable advancements in this domain include generative AI models, particularly various variations of Generative adversarial networks (GANs). Generative AI is growing as a revolutionary technology in clinical imaging, providing novel abilities for enhancing data, image improvement, and particular disease analysis. This review systematically examines more than 150 research papers published from 2018 to 2025, concentrating on the use of generative methods in key imaging techniques such as OCT, X-ray, CT, MRI, PET, retinal fundus imaging, mammography, and ultrasound. This study categorizes and compares the performance of GANs, Variational Autoencoders (VAEs), and diffusion approaches across different applications, including reconstruction of images, high resolution, noise elimination, anomaly identification, and synthetic data production for detecting diseases. The review analysis indicates that generative AI methods have shown significant enhancements in medical diagnostics, with accuracy improvements of between 5 and 20 per cent when synthetically enhanced data is utilized, and the quality of image measures increases between 15 and 40 per cent among modalities, including MRI and CT. The research presents findings indicating that diffusion approaches surpass GANs in generating excellent clinical images, although GANs maintain computational efficiency for real-time augmentation applications. Moreover, we suggest prospective avenues for future studies to address the current constraints and fulfill the changing needs of the medical field. The article summarizes the basic ideas behind generative AI, particularly its ability to produce lifelike and highly accurate visuals. Afterward, it explores each imaging technique’s particular difficulties and possibilities in diagnosing diseases.

title: Industrial defect detection for data privacy and domain differences: Based on federated learning and unsupervised domain adaptation
abstract: Industrial defect detection faces challenges from domain shifts in unsupervised domain adaptation (UDA) and data privacy in federated learning (FL). This study proposes a novel industrial defect detection method based on lightweight UDA and FL participant selection optimization (IDD-LUDA-FL), a lightweight UDA-FL framework for robust cross-domain defect detection. This method leverages MobileNet V4 for efficient feature extraction, dynamic feature pyramid network (DYFPN) for multi-scale processing, and quantized convolutional neural networks (Quantized-CNN) for model compression, while optimizing FL participant selection using Shapley values and second-order Markov chains to enhance privacy and mitigate attacks like label shuffling. Extensive studies on four industrial datasets show improved performance across a variety of source-target adaptation scenarios. Compared to other state-of-the-art methods, the proposed method achieves an average accuracy of 91%. Inference speed improves by over 50%, with detection speed reaching 58.6f/s. The holistic integration of lightweight UDA and secure FL mechanisms enables effective handling of data heterogeneity and adversarial threats, validating its utility for practical industrial applications. This work advances multi-domain defect detection, providing a foundation for scalable, privacy-preserving AI in manufacturing.

title: FiberGNN: A graph neural network framework for efficient photonic crystal fiber parameters prediction
abstract: Advancing next-generation optical technologies, from telecommunication networks to biomedical imaging, critically depends on the ability to design photonic crystal fibers (PCFs) with complex, tailored microstructures. However, this design process is severely hampered by the computationally intensive and time-consuming numerical simulations required. While machine learning has emerged as a promising alternative, existing models struggle to generalize across diverse and disordered fiber geometries due to their reliance on rigid data representations. Here, we introduce FiberGNN, a graph neural network framework that overcomes this fundamental limitation. By representing fibers as graphs, FiberGNN accurately predicts key physical parameters directly from the fiber’s microstructure and material properties, demonstrating robust generalization to both regular and disordered PCFs. To further enhance accessibility, we have developed an online platform providing real-time predictions, drastically accelerating the fiber design cycle. Our work not only offers a powerful tool for nonlinear optical systems but also presents a new paradigm for modeling complex physical systems where topological relationships are paramount.

title: Unlocking molecular optimization potential by leveraging active learning for scaffold-preserving optimization with ALMO
abstract: Molecular optimization plays a crucial role in drug discovery by improving pharmacokinetic properties and biological activity while preserving the core structure of lead compounds. However, existing methods often face challenges with limited labeled data and achieving integration into chemists’ experimental workflows. To address these challenges, we introduce ALMO (Active Learning-based Molecular Optimization), a framework designed for scaffold-preserving molecular optimization that combines active learning with evolutionary strategies. By leveraging pre-training on unlabeled datasets and fine-tuning through active learning and PPO-Clip reinforcement learning, ALMO achieves precise optimization without relying on Matched Molecular Pair (MMP) data or human annotations. Extensive experiments demonstrate that ALMO achieves superior performance across various molecular optimization scenarios, particularly under stringent structural similarity constraints. Additionally, ALMO provides enhanced interpretability and closely aligns with chemists’ practical workflows, making it a robust and effective solution for advancing drug discovery and molecular design.

title: PromptMed: Prompt-driven semi-supervised medical image classification with class-balanced consistency and contrastive learning
abstract: Existing pre-trained foundation models have demonstrated strong generalization and transfer capabilities across diverse domains. However, directly fine-tuning all parameters of pre-trained models for medical image classification requires massive labeled data, making it inefficient and resource-intensive. To address this, we aim to leverage semi-supervised learning (SSL) techniques to reduce the need for massive annotations for efficient fine-tuning. In this context, we propose PromptMed, a parameter-efficient framework for semi-supervised medical image classification, which consists of three key components: Prompt Noise Injection (PNI), Class-Balanced Prompt Adaptation (CBPA), and Contrastive Feature Consistency (CFC). Specifically, we introduce PNI to enhance the robustness of prompt representations and enable effective prompt-based consistency training. PNI applies Gaussian noise of varying strengths to prompt tokens, serving as a form of representation-level augmentation. To mitigate class imbalance, we design a CBPA mechanism that dynamically assigns higher noise to minority classes based on recent class distributions, encouraging better representation learning for hard categories. Additionally, to promote feature consistency, especially for minority and visually similar classes, we incorporate a CFC on the vision branch features. These three components work synergistically to enable PromptMed to achieve robust, balanced, and highly discriminative medical image classification with significantly reduced trainable parameters. Extensive experiments on multiple medical image datasets demonstrate that our approach achieves state-of-the-art performance while significantly reducing the number of trainable parameters.

title: Discovering minimal sets of informative genes via multi-step clustering of SRBC-tumor gene expression data using generalized self-organizing neural networks
abstract: Molecular diagnostic procedures for tumors – employing microarray technologies – become effective tools for performing precise and early diagnosis of tumors. However, informative genes, i.e., the disease relevant genes constitute only a small fraction of the overall number of the available genes. Therefore, the selection of minimal subsets of highly informative genes is essential in designing accurate tumor classification/prediction systems. This paper aims at designing a two-stage procedure for effective uncovering of collections of such genes. In the first stage of our approach, we apply our tool, i.e., generalized self-organizing neural networks (SONNs) with evolving, splitting-merging structures to the gene data clustering to detect big, dominating clusters of non-informative/noisy genes to be removed from the original data. Drastically reduced – in the first stage – gene expression data set creates an excellent point of departure for effective uncovering – in the second stage and using conventional tools (e.g., decision trees) – of different minimal subsets of highly informative genes. Our approach is able to select – out of original 2308 SRBCT genes – several 4-gene and one 3-gene subsets containing genes characterized by the highest level of informativeness that result in 100%-accuracies of categorizing particular types of tumors. A broad comparative analysis of our approach and 22 available alternative methods (providing 26 different solutions) demonstrates that our approach definitely outperforms all alternative methods in terms of uncovering gene subsets containing minimal numbers of genes characterized by the earlier-mentioned highest level of informativeness.

title: A memristive hopfield neural network under electromagnetic radiation and its application in chaos–DNA image encryption
abstract: In this study, a memristive Hopfield neural network (HNN) model under electromagnetic radiation is proposed by introducing a multi-piecewise polynomial–sinusoidal memristor and an electromagnetic coupling term. The model possesses multiple stable equilibrium point and an index-2 saddle-focus point, which induces the formation of scroll-like attractors. Dynamical analyses using phase portraits, bifurcation diagrams, and Lyapunov exponents spectra reveal diverse behaviors—including double-scroll, single-scroll limit-cycle, and transient chaotic states—as well as multistability and rich nonlinear characteristics modulated by the radiation and polynomial parameters. Building on this chaotic source, a hardware-oriented chaos–DNA fusion image encryption algorithm is designed. Chaotic sequences are employed to create an irregular minesweeper-based partition and to drive the selection of dynamic DNA-encoding rules. These processes, combined with local bit-block rotations and multi-image interleaving, achieve global permutation and bidirectional diffusion under the control of regional features. Experimental results demonstrate large key space, strong key sensitivity, near-ideal entropy, high NPCR/UACI, and robustness against noise and data loss. The proposed memristive HNN thus provides a physically realizable and efficient chaotic kernel for secure image encryption and neuromorphic information processing.

title: AnomalyLVM:Vision-language models for zero-shot anomaly detection
abstract: Zero-Shot Anomaly Detection (ZSAD) has emerged as a promising approach for identifying unseen defects without requiring annotated training samples, but existing methods typically focus only on image-level detection and overlook fine-grained pixel-level localization. To address this gap, we propose AnomalyLVM, a unified vision-language framework designed to simultaneously handle image-level classification and pixel-level segmentation in zero-shot settings. AnomalyLVM leverages frozen SAM2 and DINO-X as dual visual encoders to extract complementary spatial and semantic features, which are fused and decoded via a lightweight decoder to generate localization maps. Meanwhile, a frozen CLIP text encoder guides image-level detection through semantic similarity matching. To enhance the accuracy of pixel-wise supervision, we introduce a Feature Enhancement Module (FEM) that dynamically refines static LayerCAM maps by integrating attention cues from both visual encoders and decoder affinity signals, resulting in more consistent and context-aware pseudo labels. Additionally, we adopt a prompt-free, object-agnostic strategy that replaces handcrafted templates with learnable, generic prompts, enabling AnomalyLVM to generalize across diverse categories and defect types without relying on domain-specific knowledge. Extensive experiments conducted across 17 real-world anomaly detection datasets from industrial and medical domains indicate that AnomalyLVM outperforms other ZSAD methods and can generalize better to different categories and even domains. title: 3D-MolGL: A multimodal framework for integrating 3D molecular graphs into language models
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have exhibited remarkable capabilities in natural language generation and have been extensively applied to diverse tasks such as text generation and medical literature analysis, demonstrating robust proficiency in structured data processing and knowledge extraction. However, these models generally overlook the crucial three-dimensional (3D) molecular conformations, which are vital for understanding key chemical properties. This oversight significantly limits the potential of LLMs in the biomolecular field, particularly in complex tasks like drug structure discovery. To address this, we propose a Multimodal Framework for Integrating 3D Molecular Graphs into Language Models (3D-MolGL). It employs a Physics-Informed Equivariant Graph Neural Network (PI-EGNN) incorporating physically meaningful edge-level priors and physics-based regularization, aligning learned representations with empirical data and physical laws. Our approach incorporates an Iterative Cross-Modal Fusion module to reinforce structural and linguistic information, enabling the model to capture complex dependencies and improve the alignment between molecular data and natural language. Moreover, the Region-Phrase Semantic Grounding module enables fine-grained alignment between molecular substructures and linguistic tokens, thereby reinforcing the connection between molecular semantics and their textual representation. Additionally, the Best-of-N sampling strategy enhances output reliability. Notably, 3D-MolGL achieves competitive or state-of-the-art performance in molecule captioning and 3D-aware question answering tasks, while utilizing approximately 75% fewer parameters than existing large-scale multimodal architectures. This demonstrates that robust molecular reasoning capabilities can be achieved with more compact models, providing a promising new perspective for interpretable AI in chemistry.

title: LDM-DTI: A multimodal framework integrating pretrained language models and geometric graph networks for interpretable drug-target interaction prediction
abstract: Accurate prediction of drug-target interactions (DTIs) is essential for speeding up the discovery of new therapeutics. Although significant progress has been made with deep learning-based approaches, considerable challenges remain in learning informative molecular representations and modeling the intricate nature of drug-target associations. To overcome these limitations, an end-to-end predictive architecture, termed LDM-DTI, is proposed. In this framework, drug and protein sequences are encoded via pretrained large language models. Specifically, ChemBERTa is utilized to derive high-dimensional semantic and structural features from SMILES strings, while ProtBERT is employed to extract contextual representations from amino acid sequences. To further incorporate spatial molecular information, a three-layer Graph Convolutional Network (GCN) and an Equivariant Graph Neural Network (EGNN) are integrated to capture both 2D topological and 3D geometric characteristics of drug molecules. Protein-level features are refined through dynamic convolutional operations and multi-head self-attention mechanisms. These representations are then fused via a Dynamic Interactive Attention Module (DIAM) to model cross-modal dependencies between drugs and targets. The proposed framework demonstrates superior predictive performance and generalizability across four public benchmark datasets, consistently surpassing ten state-of-the-art baselines. Ablation experiments are conducted to quantify the contributions of individual components, and protein-level attention maps are visualized to enhance interpretability. Overall, LDM-DTI offers a robust and interpretable solution for DTI prediction, with strong potential for accelerating structure-informed drug discovery.

title: Transformer-masked autoencoder (MAE) for robust medical image classification: A comprehensive survey
abstract: Medical image classification underpins screening, diagnosis, and treatment planning, but conventional CNN pipelines remain label-hungry and brittle under noise, occlusion, and domain shift. Transformer-based masked autoencoders (MAEs) offer a compelling alternative by exploiting large unlabeled archives to learn anatomy-aware representations. This survey systematically synthesizes various studies on MAE-based encoders for X-ray, MRI, CT, ultrasound, and histopathology. We propose a modality-aware taxonomy spanning ViT/Swin backbones, masking strategies, and training regimes, and harmonize reported results against strong CNN and contrastive baselines. Across modalities, MAE initialization consistently improves label efficiency, calibration, and cross-scanner transfer, especially when combined with parameter-efficient fine-tuning. We distill practical design heuristics (mask ratios, encoder & decoder depth, PEFT rank), highlight recurrent pitfalls in evaluation and reporting, and outline future directions in domain-aware masking, scalable 3D pretraining, cross-modal co-masking, and clinically grounded interpretability. The codes for to generate the results can be found in this https://github.com/ekwadwo1/Medical-MAE-Survey.

title: Adapting vision foundation models with lightweight trident decoder for remote sensing change detection
abstract: The field of remote sensing image change detection has attracted significant interest. However, prevailing methods tend to concentrate on the basic extraction of change features, neglecting the crucial role of stable semantic patterns (e.g., ”features that remain consistent across time”) in bi-temporal images (image pairs taken at different times) for enhancing change feature extraction precision. Moreover, existing change detection networks often grapple with striking an optimal balance between accuracy and complexity. To surmount these challenges, we leverage the advanced feature extraction capabilities of pre-trained Vision Foundation Models (FastSAM), introducing an innovative lightweight Trident Decoder framework for remote sensing change detection, termed LTCD. Our framework encompasses three pioneering fully convolutional modules: the Attention-CDut Module, Trident Decoder Module, and Segment-Head Module. The Attention-CD Module enriches the semantic content of bi-temporal image features via cross-attention, which precedes the decoding phase, effectively decoupling change features. The Trident Decoder Module intensifies the influence of stable semantic patterns on change features within the feature pyramid, resulting in a distinctive trident-shaped feature output. Furthermore, the Segment-Head Module integrates shallow auxiliary tasks under a deep supervision learning scheme to bolster feature interaction. Experimental results demonstrate that our work outperforms state-of-the-art (SOTA) approaches, including both CNN-based and Transformer-based methods, across five challenging benchmark datasets, achieving improved accuracy with a model size 10  ×  smaller than previous SOTA models.

title: Psychology of phishing emails: Quantifying persuasion principles and simulating detection with large language models
abstract: Phishing remains a significant cyber threat that leverages human cognitive biases; however, quantitative models of the underlying psychological mechanisms are underdeveloped. This study first operationalizes and validates a unified psychological framework for phishing detection, quantifying how classic persuasion principles and linguistic deception cues distinguish phishing from legitimate emails. An analysis of a 340,912-sample corpus revealed that features such as sensitive requests and scarcity are the strongest independent predictors of phishing. Interaction analyses indicated predominantly antagonistic effects among paired persuasion cues. Leveraging this psychological framework, the study then tests the dual-process theory of cognition by using four LLMs as scalable cognitive proxies. Simulating a shift from heuristic (intuitive) to systematic (analytical) processing via prompting significantly increased detection accuracy from 83.09% to 88.20%. These results support dual-process accounts of phishing susceptibility, establish LLMs as effective cognitive proxies, and recommend integrating psycholinguistic features and systematic LLM ensembles into email security systems.

title: Hierarchical frequency-aware transformer for robust short- and multi-horizon photovoltaic power forecasting
abstract:
Photovoltaic (PV) power forecasting remains a challenging task due to the non-stationary, rapidly fluctuating, and multi-scale nature of solar generation. This study proposes a frequency-aware hybrid forecasting framework that integrates Wavelet Packet Decomposition (WPD), Variational Mode Decomposition (VMD), and a unified Transformer encoder for accurate PV power prediction. By decoupling frequency treatment from architectural complexity, the framework aims to improve robustness under highly variable operating conditions.

The resulting WPD-VMD-Transformer model is evaluated using real 30-minute PV production data from two photovoltaic power plants located in southern Algeria and benchmarked against widely used forecasting models, including Informer, GRU, CNN–LSTM, and XGBoost. Experimental results demonstrate notable improvements in forecasting accuracy and stability across different weather conditions and forecasting horizons, highlighting the effectiveness of hierarchical frequency-aware modeling in addressing non-stationary PV power forecasting challenges.

title: Data-driven decision support in environmental management: hybrid GNN-PINN modeling of subsurface soil temperature
abstract:
Accurate forecasting of subsurface soil temperature is essential for climate-smart agriculture, environmental monitoring, and data-driven resource management. Modern agricultural information systems increasingly depend on predictive analytics, yet conventional physics-based models require extensive calibration, and purely data-driven methods often struggle to generalize across heterogeneous landscapes. To address these limitations, this study introduces a hybrid predictive framework that integrates Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) with Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) for use within decision-support and environmental information systems. The PINN component embeds the one-dimensional heat-diffusion equation into the learning process, producing physically coherent temperature profiles without the need for detailed soil parameters. In parallel, the GNN models spatial relationships among meteorological stations by encoding geographic and topographic similarity, enabling the system to transfer knowledge across regions and improve generalization.

The model is trained and evaluated using a multi-year dataset from 15 meteorological stations across Türkiye, representing diverse climatic and soil conditions. Comparative experiments show that the hybrid GNN-PINN consistently outperforms standalone PINN, GNN-only, and multilayer perceptron baselines. Improvements are most pronounced at deeper soil layers (50–100 cm), where thermal diffusion dominates and conventional models tend to lose accuracy. Ablation analyses reveal that physics-based constraints and spatial message passing make complementary contributions, with statistically significant performance gains (p < 0.05). Despite these enhancements, the hybrid model requires only ∼ 20% additional training cost and maintains near real-time inference.

By combining physical principles with spatially aware learning, the proposed framework offers reliable, interpretable, and computationally efficient soil-temperature forecasts, supporting data-driven decision making in climate-smart agriculture and environmental management.

title: CORE: A cognitive science-inspired framework for task-adaptive reasoning enhancement in large language models
abstract: Reasoning enhancement is fundamental for advancing the performance of large language models (LLMs) in complex cognitive tasks. However, many existing prompting methods lack task adaptability; by applying uniform reasoning strategies without distinguishing problem characteristics, they often lead to a mismatch between reasoning depth and task requirements. To address these limitations, we propose Cognitive Orchestration for Reasoning Enhancement (CORE), a cognitive science theory-informed prompting framework designed to guide the reasoning process of LLMs. Drawing upon Kahneman’s dual-process theory and Dewey’s reflective thinking theory, CORE provides structured guidance through four components: Constructing Thinking Pattern, Adjusting Thinking Dimension, Organizing Reasoning Stage, and Optimizing Implementation Strategy. The framework employs prompt-embedded conditional execution to guide models in selecting appropriate reasoning stages based on problem characteristics, thereby aligning reasoning complexity with task demands. We evaluated CORE on benchmark tasks covering diverse reasoning types across four language models with distinct architectures, including Grok-4, DeepSeek-V3, GLM-4-Flash, and Doubao-1-5-Lite. Experimental results demonstrate that CORE achieves consistent improvements in average accuracy across all evaluated models, outperforming strong baselines including Chain-of-Thought, Self-Consistency, and Tree-of-Thoughts. Further analysis reveals that CORE successfully induces task-adaptive reasoning behavior, enabling models to exhibit differentiated processing patterns in response to varying problem features. Component analysis confirms that all framework parts contribute positively to performance and assume distinct roles within the overall reasoning process. These findings indicate that cognitive science-inspired prompt design offers a promising principled direction for adaptive reasoning enhancement and provides insights for constructing adaptive prompting strategies tailored to diverse task requirements.

title: Physics-Informed spatiotemporal deep learning for multivariate atmospheric forecasting
abstract: With the rapid development of the low-altitude economy, emerging applications such as general aviation, drone delivery, and urban air mobility are placing higher demands on the accurate sensing and forecasting of the low-altitude atmospheric environment. Current research faces two major challenges: (1) traditional numerical weather prediction (NWP) methods have limited responsiveness to rapid disturbances in the lower atmosphere, making them inadequate for precision requirements in low-altitude flight; and (2) data-driven deep learning methods often lack physical consistency constraints, leading to poor performance in forecasting short-term rapid fluctuations and compromising flight safety. To address these challenges, this paper proposes an innovative short-term forecasting framework for low-altitude meteorological variables, which integrates physical knowledge with short sequence modeling. First, a temporal sequence branch mechanism is introduced to precisely model the multi-scale dynamic variations in the low-altitude atmospheric field, significantly enhancing the model’s ability to detect and predict both rapid disturbances and slow-varying trends, thereby improving flight safety assurance. Second, an adaptive physics-guided loss is designed to incorporate conservation constraints, effectively improving the physical consistency of predictions and mitigating unrealistic forecasts in complex low-altitude environments. The experimental results show that the proposed method outperforms the mainstream baseline model in several metrics. Meanwhile, the model maintains stable generalization performance in different climate regions, reflecting good regional adaptability. In the distribution consistency assessment of the validation variables, such as relative humidity and wind speed, the KL divergence of the model is as low as 0.004 and 0.008, respectively, which demonstrates its good fitting ability to the actual distribution. Overall, the method in this paper achieves a good balance between prediction accuracy, physical consistency, and timeliness, and provides an effective solution for real-time weather prediction oriented to low-altitude traffic and environment sensing.

title: Unsupervised anomaly detection with a stacked transformer diffusion reconstruction framework
abstract: Reconstruction-based anomaly detection remains appealing for industrial inspection due to its ability to handle unknown defect types, yet diffusion models still suffer from semantic drift and geometric misalignment when reconstructing anomalous inputs. This paper presents STDRAD (Unsupervised Anomaly Detection with a Stacked Transformer Diffusion Reconstruction Framework), a fully transformer-based diffusion reconstruction model for unsupervised multi-class anomaly detection. Built upon the DiT paradigm, STDRAD replaces the conventional U-Net with a scalable stacked-transformer denoiser that provides global context modeling. A lightweight Adapter module is integrated into DiT blocks to improve feature modulation and facilitate faster optimization during training. To mitigate misalignment in latent diffusion, we introduce an ISKG (Isomorphic Structural Guidance) module that injects structurally compatible cues into the denoising trajectory. A multi-scale feature alignment strategy further enhances reconstruction fidelity across both textures and large structural regions. For anomaly scoring, multi-level representations extracted by a pretrained ResNet are compared between the input and its reconstruction, and their feature discrepancies are aggregated to produce anomaly maps. Extensive experiments on the MVTec AD and VisA benchmarks show that STDRAD achieves 95.8%/96.0% image/pixel-level AUROC on MVTec AD and 86.9%/97.2% on VisA, and qualitative results confirm cleaner reconstructions and more reliable suppression of anomalous patterns across diverse industrial scenarios.

title: Expert-guided forecasting of epidemic ARI incidence based on physics-informed neural networks and large language models
abstract: This paper presents an agent-based AI system that uses large-scale language models (LLMs) to dynamically adapt physically-informed neural networks (PINNs) based on high-quality expert judgment. Our system enables interactive refinement of epidemiological forecasts by translating unstructured expert feedback into structured modifications of the loss function, eliminating the need for prior mathematical formalization. Experimental results confirm the fundamental feasibility of this approach, demonstrating a success rate of 25-27% for the best models and providing a compelling proof-of-concept for using LLMs as core components of interactive decision support systems. This work represents a step toward building robust expert-led forecasting systems for public health problems, while simultaneously highlighting the need to develop more rigorous control mechanisms to ensure full robustness. The code of our system is available at https://github.com/vnleonenko/Epi_PINN_LLM.

title: Feature engineering and pruning in neural networks for urban climate instability prediction
abstract: Urban climate prediction faces significant challenges due to the complex interactions between meteorological variables and the increasing need for accurate instability forecasting. This study presents a comprehensive approach to feature engineering using 123 years (1901-2023) of daily meteorological observations from Athens, Greece, transforming five basic variables (temperature, humidity, precipitation) into 19 engineered features, which together with the original variables yield a 24-dimensional input space plus a novel Climate Instability Index. We develop and mathematically prove a pruning theorem demonstrating that removing uninformative features improves neural network performance, particularly in data-sparse regimes. Through extensive validation using 100 random train-test splits on an Artificial Neural Network with Adam optimisation, we demonstrate that pruning the least correlated feature (temp\_asymmetry, Spearman r = 0.023) consistently improves predictions. Results show that in sparse data conditions (1% of the full dataset), pruning increases R^{2} by about 9% on average and up to 47% in a single split, while maintaining performance in data-rich scenarios. Our findings establish that Spearman-based feature selection provides a robust a priori filter, offering practical guidelines for climate prediction model optimisation. The methodology demonstrates how systematic feature engineering combined with correlation-based pruning can significantly enhance urban microclimate predictions.

title: A time-frequency adaptive transformer for long-term wind power forecasting under complex meteorological fluctuations
abstract: Accurate wind power forecasting remains challenging due to complex temporal dependencies and intricate spectral characteristics induced by meteorological fluctuations. Existing data-driven forecasting models, particularly real-valued deep learning methods, often struggle to jointly model long-range temporal patterns and frequency-domain representations, and may lose intrinsic amplitude-phase information during representation learning. To address these limitations, this paper proposes a time-frequency adaptive Transformer (TFAT) model, which establishes a framework that synergizes rigorous complex-domain spectral analysis with data-driven multi-scale convolution. Specifically, a two-stage architecture is constructed to convert time-domain data into a refined frequency-domain representation using an extended Fourier transform strategy. A frequency-energy driven adaptive mechanism is then employed to dynamically allocate attention weights, effectively balancing the modeling of global trends and local fluctuations. Furthermore, by introducing complex-domain attention, the model operates directly in the complex spectrum, preserving the amplitude-phase coupling inherent in the original data. Experimental results on three real-world measurement datasets demonstrate that the proposed method significantly enhances estimation reliability. Compared with state-of-the-art comparison models, TFAT achieves reductions of approximately 8.11%-11.73% in root mean squared error, 5.17%-8.71% in mean absolute error, and 8.11%-11.70% in relative squared error, highlighting its robustness and effectiveness for wind power forecasting under complex meteorological fluctuations.

title: HTMNet: A hybrid transformer-mamba network for LiDAR-based 3D detection and semantic segmentation
abstract: LiDAR-based 3D detection and semantic segmentation are fundamental tasks for autonomous driving and mobile robotics, yet their performance is often constrained by the extreme sparsity of point cloud data and significant intra-class variations. In this paper, we propose a Hybrid Transformer-Mamba Network (HTMNet), which integrates 3D sparse convolutions, Global Channel Attention (GCA), and a Mamba state-space block to jointly capture local geometric features, inter-channel dependencies, and long-range contextual relationships. This hybrid design enhances feature representation while preserving computational efficiency. Embedded within a U-shaped encoder-decoder architecture, our HTMNet effectively leverages voxelized LiDAR information to construct richer hierarchical representations. Experimental results demonstrate that our HTMNet achieves state-of-the-art (SOTA) performance on the large-scale JRDB pedestrian dataset for the 3D detection task, with an Average Precision (AP) of 48.5%. Similarly, it delivers competitive results on the SemanticKITTI dataset for the 3D semantic segmentation task, achieving a mean Intersection over Union (mIoU) of 73.5%. In addition, our HTMNet runs at 38 Frames Per Second (FPS) on a single NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5090 GPU. These results highlight the effectiveness of our HTMNet in capturing both local geometry and global context in sparse point clouds, thereby improving the performance of 3D object detection and semantic segmentation. The project is publicly available at https://github.com/jinzhengguang/HTMNet.

title: Unveiling the complementary synergy of CLIP and diffusion models for weakly supervised semantic segmentation
abstract: Weakly supervised semantic segmentation (WSSS) relies solely on image-level labels, deriving Class Activation Maps (CAMs) as pixel-level seeds and converting them into pseudo labels for segmentation. Recently, methods have leveraged either Contrastive Language-Image Pretraining (CLIP) or diffusion models to generate CAMs within WSSS pipelines. However, how to combine these two paradigms within a single framework remains underexplored. In this work, we propose ComCD (Complementary synergy of CLIP and Diffusion models), which integrates these two paradigms and leverages their complementarity to improve CAM quality. First, class-specific CAMs are derived from the CLIP branch and the diffusion model branch. Second, we design an entropy-based fusion that maps the entropy difference between the two CAMs to reliability weights, fuses them into a refined CAM, and converts it into a pseudo mask. Third, a trainable segmentation network with a logit gating module predicts weights to fuse the two branches and produces the final segmentation. Experimental results demonstrate the superiority of the proposed ComCD over recent state-of-the-art methods in both WSSS and open-vocabulary semantic segmentation.

title: Enhancing open world object detection via learning class-agnostic foundational attributes with large language models
abstract: Open World Object Detection (OWOD) requires the detector to continually recognize and adapt to novel objects beyond the training distribution. Existing methods often rely on large language models (LLMs) to describe the visual attributes of known classes and use these attributes to identify potential objects. However, this dependence on known class semantics introduces category bias, thereby limiting generalization to unseen classes. In this paper, we propose a novel OWOD method, OW-CFA, which learns class-agnostic foundational attributes to enable robust and interpretable detection of both known and unknown objects. Specifically, we leverage LLMs to construct an initial class-agnostic attribute space that captures general visual cues such as color and shape. Given the redundancy inherent in the initial attribute space, we propose Asymmetric Attribute Response (AAR) to enhance discriminative activations for target classes, establishing a more robust attribute-to-class mapping. Furthermore, we propose Entropy-Regularized Attribute Sparsification (ERAS), which leverages low-entropy regularization to enhance semantic interpretability and improve generalization to unknown classes. To estimate the confidence of unknown objects, we propose an Unknown Probability Estimation (UPE) that integrates in-distribution correlation with out-of-distribution likelihood. Extensive evaluations on the Real-World Object Detection (RWD) benchmark across diverse application domains validate that OW-CFA achieves a 6.1 mAP absolute gain in unknown object detection compared to state-of-the-art (SOTA) methods.

title: CoLPAT-AMP: A Transformer-Based framework for Designing novel antimicrobial peptides with property Awareness and partially controllable length
abstract: The World Health Organization warns that antimicrobial resistance (AMR) poses a global threat to public health and calls for the discovery of new antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) as potential therapeutic alternatives. Artificial intelligence (AI) revolutionized the search for AMPs, yet existing generative models like those based on GANs or diffusion often lack systematic evaluation of trade-offs between fidelity, novelty, and diversity. Moreover, sequence length is rarely treated as an explicit controllable design parameter. Here, we propose CoLPAT-AMP, a Transformer-based expert system enabling partial control over sequence length in AMP generation. Two complementary models were implemented and compared: (1) a conditioned model, which integrates ESM-2 embeddings with physicochemical property and sequence length conditioning during training (without explicit property specification at inference), and (2) an unconditioned model, trained solely on AMP sequences. The conditioned model achieved lower reconstruction loss (0.99 vs. 1.73), higher reconstruction accuracy (0.70 vs. 0.53), novelty (1 vs. 0.85), and greater diversity. While the overlap between physicochemical properties of generated sequences and real AMPs was stronger for the unconditioned model, indicating higher adherence to the training dataset distribution. An independent AMP classifier further confirmed that the main portion of the generated sequences by both models maintained antimicrobial characteristics. These findings suggest that the conditioned model enables partial control and expands exploration toward more diversity, while the unconditioned model emphasizes property fidelity. Overall, CoLPAT-AMP provides a property-aware, and partially length-controllable framework for rational AMP design, advancing AI-driven strategies to explore peptide space and combat antimicrobial resistance.

title: An explainable machine learning-based scoring function using interpretable features and model explanation approaches for binding affinity prediction
abstract: Although machine learning (ML)-based scoring functions (SFs) have achieved great success in structure-based drug discovery, most of them work as black boxes and lack explainability. Since explainable ML-based SFs can build user trust and reveal underlying structure–activity relationships, there is a growing need to develop ML-based SFs that are accompanied by explanations. In this study, we propose a gradient-boosted decision tree (GBDT)-based SF called XBTScore for protein–ligand binding affinity prediction. To gain the explainability of this ML-based SF, we focus on two main aspects. First, we employ seventy-two human-interpretable features as the input features, aiming to capture the enthalpic and entropic effects within protein–ligand interactions. Second, we employ SHAP to provide explanations for the integrated GBDT model. The experimental results demonstrate that compared with existing SFs, the proposed SF achieves competitive scoring power. XBTScore achieves promising scoring power, with a Pearson correlation coefficient of 0.804 on the CASF-2016 benchmark dataset. Furthermore, we analyze both the model’s predictive performance and its global and local explanations. The results suggest that both predictive accuracy and explainability should be considered in the development of ML-based SFs. XBTScore is a novel ML-based SF for high-accuracy, explainable protein–ligand binding affinity predictions.

title: Bridging distributional mismatch: Physics-informed signal adaptation and omni-dimensional dynamic calibration for non-stationary bearing fault diagnosis
abstract: Bearing vibration signals in harsh industrial environments are fundamentally non-stationary and often submerged in strong background noise. This creates a severe distributional mismatch where conventional physical priors fail to converge, while standard static deep learning models lack the adaptability to capture weak transient impulses. To bridge this gap, this paper proposes a two-stage adaptive diagnosis framework (PICA-Net) that unifies vibration analysis under a non-stationary time-series perspective. Unlike existing methods that treat denoising and diagnosis as separate tasks, PICA-Net establishes a coupled Rectify-and-Calibrate paradigm. At the input stage, we propose a Physics-informed Factorized Temporal Mixer (FTM). Instead of passive reconstruction, FTM functions as an active statistical rectifier. Under physics-informed end-to-end supervision (kurtosis and envelope sparsity), it biases the signal statistics away from noise-dominated Gaussianity toward more leptokurtic and quasi-stationary characteristics, thereby making the downstream physical priors effective under severe noise. Building upon these rectified statistics, the feature stage introduces an Omni-dimensional Dynamic Channel and Block Attention Module (ODCBAM). It tackles the residual non-stationarity that static filters cannot handle by generating sample-wise adaptive weights across spatial, filter, and kernel dimensions. This allows the model to dynamically track the transient impulses emphasized by the FTM. Extensive experiments on PU and JNU datasets demonstrate the framework’s superior robustness. Specifically, PICA-Net achieves an average F1-score of 96.78% on the JNU dataset, outperforming state-of-the-art baselines by 1.91%, and maintains over 80% accuracy even under extreme noise conditions (-8 dB). Visualization analysis further confirms that FTM significantly restores signal impulsiveness (Kurtosis: 2.49  →  4.13), validating the synergistic gain of physics-informed adaptation.

title: Task-specific models vs. large vision-language models in medical visual question answering: A survey
abstract: Medical Visual Question Answering (Med-VQA) is an emerging interdisciplinary task that integrates computer vision and natural language processing to enable automated clinical decision support based on medical images. Recent advances in deep learning have led to two prominent model paradigms: task-specific models (TSMs), which are tailored to specific datasets and clinical tasks, and large vision-language models (VLMs), which leverage large-scale pretraining to achieve strong generalization across modalities. However, a comprehensive and comparative understanding of these two approaches remains lacking. This survey presents the first systematic comparison between TSMs and VLMs in the Med-VQA domain. An unified taxonomy is introduced covering architectural strategies, knowledge integration techniques, pretraining methods, and interpretability mechanisms. Over 50 representative models are reviewed and benchmark their performance across multiple datasets. Furthermore, this paper analyses the trade-offs between accuracy, generalizability, interpretability, and computational efficiency, and examine common challenges such as hallucination, modality bias, and data scarcity. Finally, the paper outlines emerging trends and future directions, including hybrid TSM-VLM systems, instruction tuning, and trustworthy VQA frameworks, to guide the development of clinically viable Med-VQA solutions.

title: A novel PRESAF-Hopfield neural network and its DNA encryption algorithm for voice encryption
abstract: The optimization of dynamic characteristics of Hopfield neural networks (HNNs) has emerged as a prominent research hotspot in the field of brain-inspired computing, where most existing hyperchaotic HNN systems rely heavily on memristors for their realization. Addressing the issues of insufficient research on HNN activation functions and the inherent limitations of the tanh activation function of the traditional HNNs, a novel piecewise root-regularized power-exponential saturating activation function (PRESAF) is proposed in this work, and the proposed PRESAF serves as a gradient-optimized alternative to the tanh function. Based on the PRESAF, a new PRESAF-HNN mathematical model is derived, and a four-dimensional PRESAF-HNN hyperchaotic model is constructed, and its dynamic behaviors are detailed analyzed. Moreover, the physical feasibility of the system’s phase portraits is also verified on an FPGA platform. Furthermore, a PRESAF-HNN-based DNA encryption algorithm is designed and applied for voice signal encryption, and the security analyses of the PRESAF-HNN-based DNA encryption algorithm are also performed. This study provides novel insights into the optimization of HNN activation functions and the engineering applications of hyperchaotic systems.

title: 3D SeisSeg-CL: Hierarchical clustering and field seismic guided contrastive learning for robust salt body segmentation
abstract: With the advancement of high-precision exploration technologies, salt structures in deep land and marine environments have become strategic targets for hydrocarbon exploration. However, significant domain discrepancies between synthetic and field seismic data hinder the generalization of salt identification methods. This paper proposes a Hierarchical Clustering and Field Seismic Guided Contrastive Learning framework (3D SeisSeg-CL) for robust salt body segmentation. The framework includes an upstream task for image-level representation learning and a downstream task for voxel-wise prediction. The upstream task introduces a seismic cube clustering-guided strategy to enhance geological discrimination via visual clustering, entropy regularization, and semantic consistency constraints. A field seismic-guided fine-grained semantic understanding strategy with a triple-domain contrastive loss is designed to align features across domains while preserving their distinct characteristics. For the downstream task, a geology-aware 3D segmentation network incorporates a Multi-GeoAttribute Calculation (MGAC) module and a multi-scale fusion module, integrating dip-curvature-amplitude attributes to disentangle features and balance global-local information. By integrating dip-curvature-amplitude attributes to disentangle the feature space and adopting a grouped fusion mechanism to balance global structures and boundary texture details, the network significantly enhances geometric modeling capability. Through collaborative optimization on synthetic and field seismic data, an end-to-end 3D salt body segmentation model is achieved, attaining 91.7% IoU on the SEAM synthetic dataset with only 1/32 of the labels. Experiments demonstrate that the proposed contrastive learning framework enables various data-driven models to achieve excellent generalization performance on the Netherlands F3 and L3 field work areas with minimal guidance from synthetic data for salt segmentation tasks.

title: Attributes enhanced representation learning with large language model for cold-start knowledge tracing
abstract: Knowledge Tracing is a core component of modern online learning and intelligent tutoring systems, supporting personalized education through dynamic modeling of learners’ knowledge states. Nevertheless, its effectiveness is often limited by the cold-start problem. In the cold-start knowledge tracing scenarios, individual learners have extremely limited learning sequence data to train the model, which restricts the model’s ability to accurately model their knowledge state. To address the above problem, this paper proposes an attribute enhanced representation learning framework with large language models for cold-start knowledge tracing. The proposed approach begins by leveraging a dynamic modular prompting mechanism to extract multi-dimensional conceptual attributes from large language models, which are then used to project the sparse interaction sequences of cold-start learners into multiple attribute-enhanced subspaces. Moreover, a dual-view contrastive learning architecture is implemented to reduce the hallucinations and redundant information for large language models. Under this way, limited data is effectively enriched with additional high-quality concept attributes information, thereby significantly improving the performance for cold-start knowledge tracing. Extensive experiments demonstrate that, on the ASSIST09, NIPS34, and Algebra05 datasets, the proposed method achieves improvements of 7.7% and 8.2%, 6.2% and 5.8%, and 4.7% and 5.6% over the state-of-the-art model in terms of AUC and ACC, respectively, thereby establishing a new benchmark for cold-start knowledge tracing.

title: RSE-PINN: A physics-informed deep learning framework for peak particle velocity prediction in open-pit blasting
abstract: Accurate prediction of peak particle velocity (PPV) is essential for ensuring blasting safety and controlling vibration effects, which are of great importance in open-pit mining and rock engineering. However, traditional data-driven machine learning models often suffer from poor generalization, strong data dependency, and limited physical interpretability, restricting their reliability under complex geological and blasting conditions. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a physics-informed deep learning framework, termed RSE-PINN, which integrates physical constraints with data-driven modeling to achieve accurate and physically consistent PPV prediction. First, a residual network combined with a squeeze-and-excitation (SE) attention module (ResNet-SE) is constructed to enhance feature extraction and improve the model’s sensitivity to key input factors. Second, physics-based constraints derived from the Sadovsky equation and monotonicity principles are incorporated into the loss function to ensure that the predicted PPV follows physical attenuation laws. Finally, Optuna-based automated hyperparameter optimization is employed to enhance training efficiency and model robustness, and an integrated visualization platform is developed to support real-time prediction and engineering application. Field experiments demonstrate that the proposed RSE-PINN significantly outperforms conventional machine learning models in prediction accuracy. Specifically, RSE-PINN achieves an R^{2} of 0.936, RMSE of 0.343, MAE of 0.288, and MAPE of 17.5%. Compared with the average performance of seven traditional machine learning models, R^{2} increases by 15.0%, while RMSE, MAE, and MAPE decrease by 44.3%, 43.6%, and 19.6%, respectively. Compared with the baseline ResNet, R^{2} improves by 8.9%, and RMSE, MAE, and MAPE decrease by 35.4%, 33.3%, and 10.8%, respectively. This study provides a novel and physically interpretable deep learning framework for reliable PPV prediction, offering valuable insights for vibration control and design optimization in rock mechanics and rock engineering.

title: Adaptive probabilistic transformer for medical image segmentation
abstract: Transformer architectures have become increasingly prominent in medical image segmentation due to their self-attention mechanisms that effectively model global dependencies and long-range spatial relationships. However, the standard dot-product attention that underlies these architectures suffers from interconnected limitations that impair clinical performance. Specifically, dot-product attention exhibits high vulnerability to imaging noise and artifacts common in medical images. Additionally, its fixed scaling parameters cannot adapt to the diverse discrimination requirements of different anatomical structures, from fine-grained tumor boundaries to homogeneous organ regions. Furthermore, conventional skip connections in encoder-decoder architectures create semantic inconsistencies that further compromise segmentation accuracy. To address these challenges, we propose APFormer, a novel encoder-decoder architecture that incorporates Adaptive Probabilistic Attention (APA) and Triple-Domain Skip Connections (TDSC). The APA mechanism replaces standard dot-product attention with a probabilistic kernel based on exponential negative squared Euclidean distance. This enables dynamic modulation of discrimination sensitivity across different anatomical regions while incorporating entropy-guided sparse key selection to suppress noise and enhance signal-to-noise ratio. The TDSC module addresses semantic gaps through integrated spatial, channel, and feature domain attention mechanisms. Extensive experiments on Synapse, ACDC, SegTHOR, ISIC2017, ISIC2018, and PH2 datasets demonstrate that our method effectively balances precise boundary delineation with noise robustness, achieving superior segmentation performance across diverse anatomical structures.
