title: Prediction of key parameters in aquaculture biofilters using a physics-informed spatial self-attention gated recurrent unit model
abstract: Data-driven modelling is essential in aquaculture, especially for complex systems where internal environmental conditions and reaction mechanisms are difficult to describe accurately. However, the black-box nature and high data dependency of traditional data-driven models limit their practical applicability. To address these challenges, we propose a physics-informed spatial self-attention gated recurrent (PSAG) unit model that integrates process data with domain-specific physical constraints. The spatial self-attention (SSA) module extracts key features from the process data through convolutional operations weighted by attention scores, which are then passed to the gated recurrent unit (GRU) for spatial prediction. The model was validated using data from an aquaculture biofilter system. Results showed that the spatial self-attention GRU framework performs well under conditions of limited data and significant distribution shifts, and that the inclusion of physical constraints could further improve predictive accuracy.

title: PSTG-Net: A physics-informed spatiotemporal multimodal dynamic graph network for wind power forecasting
abstract: Accurate wind power forecasting is essential for the stable integration of renewable energy into modern power grids and for effective operational planning. But most existing forecasting models do not consider the combined effects of cloud physics and boundary-layer wind processes, and also do not consider the spatiotemporal dependencies between different modes of meteorological data. This creates a gap in research on the consistency of physical models for multi-modal wind prediction. To overcome these shortcomings, the current work aims to create an innovative deep learning framework that can integrate atmospheric physics and spatiotemporal modelling for better wind power forecasting. This work presents the PSTG-Net, a physics-informed spatiotemporal multimodal dynamic graph network for wind power forecasting, a novel architecture that synergistically combines atmospheric physics with advanced multi-modal machine learning through three fundamental advancements. Methodologically, the proposed approach consists of three core components, the physics-constrained cloud-wind interaction module enhances satellite-based wind retrieval by modeling cloud microphysics’ impact on boundary-layer winds through radiative transfer corrections and momentum parameterizations. The multi-modal dynamic graph representation module innovatively processes temporal wind sequences via dynamically evolving recurrent graphs while concurrently analyzing spatial wind field structures through adaptive similarity graphs, both seamlessly integrated with remote sensing observations. The spatiotemporal-physical fusion graph attention network module implements a sophisticated attention mechanism that intelligently weights and combines temporal patterns, spatial relationships, and image-derived features while rigorously maintaining physical consistency. Experiments are done on the real-world wind farm data. The PSTG-Net has a 32.7% lower error than the best benchmarks, and it captures complicated interactions between clouds and winds and spatiotemporal patterns well. In conclusion, PSTG-Net gives a complete solution which at the same time resolves cloud-wind interaction, spatiotemporal dependency, and cross-modal feature fusion inside one single framework, it has great practical value for renewable energy management and grid operation.

title: Self -adaptive neural networks for domain generalization in medical image segmentation
abstract: Domain generalization is a critical challenge for expert systems in real-world medical environments, where data distributions often vary across acquisition settings. Existing domain generalization methods typically rely on carefully designed data augmentation or lack adaptivity to new data, which limits their applicability to new datasets. To address this problem, we propose a Self-Adaptive Neural Network (SA-Net) that learns domain-insensitive yet instance-adaptive feature representations. The proposed framework introduces a lightweight self-adaptive generator to rectify feature representations at the instance level and combines it with adversarial domain learning to suppress domain-specific information. Furthermore, a novel sample error loss is designed to improve the training of the self-adaptive generator by enforcing that removing the rectified latent representation from the original feature representation does not affect the final segmentation output. The effectiveness of SA-Net is validated on three representative medical image segmentation tasks, i.e., eye vessel segmentation, optic disc/cup segmentation, and skin lesion segmentation, across 12 datasets with substantial domain diversity. Experimental results demonstrate that SA-Net consistently outperforms state-of-the-art domain generalization methods on unseen domains while maintaining competitive computational efficiency.

title: Underwater acoustic semantic communication spectrum intelligent sensing algorithm based on transformer and VMamba
abstract: The complex and dynamic underwater acoustic environment results in uneven spectrum allocation, resource scarcity, and low utilization efficiency, severely hindering data transmission. This paper proposes an intelligent spectrum sensing algorithm for underwater acoustic semantic communication. The algorithm integrates Transformer and VMamba to synergistically enhance spectrum efficiency. First, an underwater acoustic semantic communication system is established. It employs a Transformer-based semantic knowledge base with relative positional encoding. The self-attention layer is replaced by a lightweight feed-forward network. This design enables more flexible representation of sequential structural information. It also enhances contextual understanding and significantly reduces parameters. Second, VMamba serves as the core reasoning engine for building a spectrum sensor. Its structured state space and cross-scanning mechanism enable efficient reasoning of spectrum occupancy status. This process utilizes time–frequency images as input. The output provides high-precision environmental sensing for dynamic access decisions. Experimental results show the semantic model’s average Bilingual Evaluation Understudy (BLEU) score is 38% higher than the Joint Source-Channel Coding (JSCC) model. The proposed VMamba sensing algorithm outperforms the energy detection, Swin Transformer (Swin-T), Data-Efficient Image Transformer (DeiT), Vision Transformer (ViT), and Convolutional Network Net Generation (ConvNeXt) algorithms. It achieves 8% higher average accuracy, 10% higher detection probability, and 13% lower false alarm probability.

title: PI-DeepOKAN: Physics-informed deep operator kolmogorov– arnold network with output-head reweighting for multiphase flow prediction
abstract: Reservoir simulation provides a fundamental framework for analyzing subsurface flow processes. In recent years, surrogate modeling has been widely investigated to enhance the efficiency of reservoir simulation. However, existing data-driven reservoir surrogate models tend to exhibit limited generalization under small-sample settings. In this paper, we propose PI-DeepOKAN, a physics-informed deep operator Kolmogorov-Arnold network with output-head reweighting for multiphase flow surrogate modeling. The model integrates Kolmogorov-Arnold networks with learnable activations to improve expressive power. It further employs a dual-branch deep operator architecture enhanced by output-head reweighting, which adaptively reweights the geological and control branches for output-specific fusion. Physical constraints are incorporated into the loss as soft penalties to enhance physical consistency under limited observations. Validation results on two datasets show that the proposed method outperforms mainstream neural networks in terms of key metrics such as coefficient of determination R^{2}, relative L_{2} error, and root mean square error (RMSE). Compared with best-performing baseline on the public faulted reservoir dataset, the proposed method reduces the relative L_{2} error by 65.2% for pressure and 63.3% for water saturation, and reduces RMSE by 64.7% for pressure and 63.4% for water saturation. These results indicate that PI-DeepOKAN is a promising approach for accurate and robust surrogate modeling of multiphase flow in complex reservoirs.

title: ES-PINN: Environment sensing-based physics-informed neural network for spectral reconstruction from RGB images
abstract: Reconstructing spectral information from single RGB images under varying illumination conditions poses significant challenges and limits the generalization capabilities of existing algorithms. To address these issues, a novel environment sensing module, Relative Spectral Power Distribution Estimation (RSPDE), is introduced and integrated into the proposed Environment Sensing-based Physics-Informed Neural Network (ES-PINN). The RSPDE leverages Retinex theory and employs virtual time frames alongside light field phase modulation techniques to simulate multi-level exposure levels. These spatiotemporal illumination features are subsequently fused using LMS-weighted methods to generate illumination images that align with the perceptual capabilities of the human visual system. A Vision-Long Short-Term Memory (Vision-LSTM) network is then adopted to regress these images to spectral power distributions (SPDs), providing essential illumination data for the reconstruction task. Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) are utilized to transform the integral process of spectral imaging into a differential process, ensuring the physical consistency of the reconstruction model and enhancing generalization across diverse illumination conditions. Additionally, an extensive SPDs library encompassing 19 commonly used light sources is constructed for robust benchmarking, and comprehensive experimental validations are conducted to demonstrate the effectiveness of the method on multiple benchmark datasets.

title: Interpretable deep learning framework for monthly rainfall prediction using attention and channel sparsity transformer model
abstract: Forecasting monthly precipitation is essential for the administration of water resources as well as the mitigation of hydrological disasters. To conduct a multi-step precipitation forecast and identify the principal determinants influencing rainfall, this model introduced an Adaptive Gated Attention Transformer (AGAT) for rainfall prediction utilizing using historical rainfall time-series data. Furthermore, the advancement of deep learning (DL) techniques has led to the formation and implementation of numerous neural network models in this domain. The two predominant models for predicting monthly rainfall are the Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU) and bidirectional Long Short Term Memory (LSTM) network. Initially, this method involves data pre-processing using data cleaning, min–max normalization and handling missing values to prepare time series input. From the pre-processed data, capture the temporal dependencies by using one dimensional Spatio temporal Bi-directional Gated Recurrent Unit (1DST-BiGRU). The residual global guided attention model is used to improve learning efficiency by concentrating on pertinent time steps. Moreover, sparsity aware global channel Assisted Vision Transformer (SAGL-ViT) introduces a sparsity based gating process that assigns feature weights dynamically to lagged rainfall features and thus effectively achieves feature selection by focusing on the most significant temporal patterns. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) are used for quantifying the significance of each lagged feature in the prediction task and enhancing interpretability. The experimental result of the proposed model was assessed by using the “Rainfall in India” datasets. The evaluation outcome shows that the suggested scheme has obtained superior outcomes of error metrics like mean square error (MSE), mean absolute error (MAE), root mean square error (RMSE) and R square (R2) values of 0.0159, 0.0147, 0.0138, and 0.9, respectively.

title: Realistic detection and prediction of autonomic nervous system anomalies: A hybrid deep learning framework with multiple optical fiber sensor fusion
abstract: Optical fiber sensors (OFS) have important applications in vital signs monitoring, especially in monitoring heart rate variability (HRV) and autonomic nervous system activity. However, it is inconvenient for long-term autonomic nervous system anomaly detection and prediction of people with optical fiber sensing. Moreover, it is hard to detect anomalies in HRV data to provide real-time previews about vital signs for doctors. To tackle these issues, we propose a hybrid deep learning-based long-term HRV anomaly detection and prediction framework with a multiple OFS fusion system, termed THCADP. The proposed multiple OFS fusion system comprises different sensor nodes for data acquisition and processing. And in THCADP, an innovative multi-graph module based on graph convolution is put forward to extract the spatial–temporal features of HRV data comprehensively, and a cross-view prediction module based on neurological constant differential equations is also proposed for extracting the complex mode exist in the multi-sensor information source better. In addition, a total of 4000 patients with different types of tumors are enrolled to develop and train our framework. The average accuracy (ACC), precision and recall of experiments reach 95.2%, 93.5% and 95.8%, respectively, demonstrating its feasibility and effectiveness, which not only exhibits better performance, but also is more outstanding when compared with the state-of-the-art approaches. We also conducted real-world clinical evaluation from two hospitals consists of 200 tumor patients, the THCADP framework achieves an ACC of 96.5% and an area under the curve (AUC) of 98.5%, which verify the proposed framework is effective and essential. THCADP can efficiently fuses information from different data of OFS fusion for various conditions and has the potential to improve the quality of medical services and human healthcare monitoring.

title: Integrating foundation models with capsule networks for enhanced weakly-supervised semantic segmentation
abstract: Weakly-Supervised Semantic Segmentation (WSSS) strives to achieve dense pixel-level predictions using only image-level annotations, thereby alleviating the need for expensive manual labeling. However, prevailing WSSS methods, often reliant on Class Activation Maps (CAMs), typically generate incomplete and inaccurate pseudo-labels that consequently limit segmentation accuracy. The recent emergence of powerful Large Pre-trained Models like CLIP, SAM, and Grounding-DINO offers new opportunities to overcome the limitations of traditional pseudo-labels in WSSS. This paper introduces a novel framework that synergistically integrates these foundational models with a capsule network module for enhanced performance. A high-quality pseudo-label generation pipeline is first developed by combining Grounding-DINO’s detection with SAM’s segmentation, prompted by both boxes and CAM-derived points. Concurrently, SAM’s structural priors are leveraged to guide a more robust affinity learning process. Finally, a capsule network with dynamic routing is introduced to learn structured object representations, whose prediction is fused with the main decoder’s output to further boost segmentation accuracy. Extensive experiments conducted on PASCAL VOC 2012 and MS COCO 2014 benchmarks demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method. Specifically, our framework achieves 79.0%/78.7% mIoU on the PASCAL VOC val/test sets and 57.5% mIoU on MS COCO val set, respectively. Code is available at https://github.com/mm10811/FMCaps.

title: Beyond vision-only anomaly detection: DualAD-LLM by leveraging large language model with dual-detector model for leather defect inspection
abstract: Anomaly detection in industrial leather inspection has become increasingly important in computer vision and manufacturing, as it enables the identification of subtle surface defects that critically impact material quality and market value. Although advanced models such as EfficientAD and PatchCore have achieved promising results, their independent operation often neglects complementary information, leading to suboptimal decision boundaries. To address this limitation, a novel anomaly detection framework is proposed that integrates EfficientAD and PatchCore through a Large Language Model (LLM)-based score fusion strategy, namely Dual Anomaly Detection with LLM Fusion (DualAD-LLM). In the proposed approach, anomaly scores from both models are considered, and the LLM generates a fused probability-like score that captures nonlinear dependencies between detection methods. This fused score is further concatenated with the original features and classified using KNN, SVM, and neural networks under a 5-fold cross-validation protocol. Experiments conducted on a self-collected leather patch dataset comprising 250 defective and non-defective samples demonstrate that the LLM-based fusion consistently enhances performance, achieving up to 97.2% accuracy and F1-score. Comprehensive analyses confirm both the discriminative strength and interpretability of the proposed method. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first study to introduce LLM-based feature generation for anomaly detection in leather inspection. These findings suggest that the proposed framework offers a promising and explainable strategy for advancing automatic quality control in the leather industry.

title: PlanetNet -MMG: A robust multi-modal graph-based deep learning model for exoplanet candidate classification
abstract: The search for exoplanets has advanced into the era of intelligent automation, yet most deep learning pipelines remain constrained to single-modality inputs or isolated views of astronomical data. We present PlanetNet-MMG, a novel multi-modal deep learning architecture that combines structured stellar metadata, raw lightcurve sequences, and graph-based relational context into a unified classification model. Our approach fuses three powerful encoders: a Tabular Transformer for domain-aware feature projection, a PatchGRU enhanced with a Vision Transformer (ViT) for learning fine-grained temporal patterns in segmented lightcurve patches, and a Graph PARE encoder that models inter-object similarity via a relational graph. Trained on a harmonized dataset derived from Kepler, TESS, and confirmed exoplanet archives, PlanetNet-MMG outperforms all state-of-the-art baselines, achieving a peak test accuracy of 90.4% and a class-averaged AUC of 0.973. Extensive experiments across 10-100 epochs and comparative evaluations against Astronet, ExoNet, OsbornNet, GCN (Lu), and ExoMiner confirm the effectiveness of our multimodal fusion. We further provide interpretability through attention overlays, t-SNE projections, and confidence histograms, reinforcing PlanetNet-MMG’s transparency and reliability for scientific discovery in astrophysics.

title: From Heuristics to Deep Generative Models: A Critical Review of Protein Sequence Analysis Architectures for Clinical Decision Support Systems (CDSS)
abstract:
The exponential growth of protein sequence data has created a critical translational gap: despite remarkable advances from heuristic aligners to deep generative models, integration of these tools into Clinical Decision Support Systems (CDSS) remains impeded by unresolved tensions between accuracy, interpretability, biosecurity, and clinical scalability. This review provides a critical, architecture-centric evaluation of protein sequence analysis methods—from alignment-based heuristics and profile HMMs to protein language models (PLMs), multi-track attention, and generative diffusion frameworks—systematically mapping each paradigm to core CDSS components. We identify that the field’s shift toward multimodal representation learning and generative AI, while transformative for structure prediction and de novo design, introduces three interconnected translational barriers: prohibitive computational cost, black-box opacity, and emerging dual-use biosecurity risks that current benchmarks fail to capture.

As our central contribution, we propose a novel two-tiered Decision Support System (DSS) architecture engineered to overcome these barriers. First, a comprehensive decision-making framework enables rational tool selection based on biological objective, data availability, computational resources, and interpretability requirements. Second, a corresponding operational architecture integrates four innovations: (i) a mandatory Proactive Biosafety Screening module enforcing computational toxicity risk assessment for all de novo designs; (ii) a Fuzzy Uncertainty Module designed to quantify ambiguity and noise in high-throughput omics data; (iii) a Multi-modal Standardization Layer that resolves data friction by unifying heterogeneous signals; and (iv) a Dual-Mode Interpretability (DMI) module bridging algorithmic explanations with biologically grounded mechanistic justification.

We further introduce CDSS-aware evaluation criteria—including metrics to measure interpretability and trust, biosafety and ethical design, clinical efficiency and scalability, and generative design validation—addressing critical limitations of community benchmarks (CASP, CAFA, CAMEO). By reframing protein informatics through the lens of responsible clinical translation, this review provides both a conceptual roadmap and practical blueprint for accelerating precision medicine, drug discovery, and synthetic biology.

title: A domain-aware deep learning framework for unified seismic analysis: integrating frequency-spatial-temporal features with trace attention
abstract: Current deep learning paradigms for seismic data processing often rely on adapting computer vision or sequence models, effectively treating seismic records as standard 2D images or 1D time series. However, such approaches frequently overlook the complex, coupled nature of seismic wavefields, which inherently span spatial, temporal, and frequency dimensions. To overcome these limitations, this study presents a novel and unified framework MDITA-Net (Multi-Domain based Inter-Trace Attention Network) designed to respect the physical characteristics of seismic acquisition. We introduce a dual-branch architecture comprising a Multi-Domain Feature Decomposition (MDFD) mechanism and an Inter-Trace Self-Attention (ITSA) module. The MDFD specifically disentangles input data into separate time, space, and frequency representations, extracting domain-specific features before synthesizing them via adaptive fusion. Concurrently, the ITSA module moves beyond local receptive fields by treating traces as interactive tokens, thereby capturing both local geological continuity and long-range structural dependencies. By integrating these components, the proposed framework serves as a versatile backbone for diverse geophysical tasks. Extensive experiments on synthetic and field datasets demonstrate that our approach significantly surpasses conventional single-domain baselines in both seismic random noise attenuation and impedance inversion tasks, proving the efficacy of explicitly modeling multi-domain interactions and trace correlations.

title: DMoE-LLM: A dual-branch mixture-of-experts framework with large language models for wind power forecasting
abstract: Accurate wind power forecasting is essential for grid stability, yet existing LLM-based methods predominantly adopt single-branch architectures lacking specialized temporal encoders, while conventional deep learning approaches do not leverage pre-trained representations. A cross-attention fusion mechanism combines complementary features from both branches, followed by a sparse mixture-of-experts decoder with top-K routing that scales model capacity through conditional expert activation. Multi-resolution forecasting heads with adaptive scheduling enable flexible multi-horizon predictions without retraining. Experiments on six wind farm datasets from geographically distinct regions demonstrate that DMoE-LLM consistently outperforms 18 baseline methods, achieving cumulative MAE reductions of 18.6%–40.8% over the strongest non-LLM baseline and 9.9% over the best LLM-based baseline across all forecasting horizons. Ablation studies confirm the independent contribution of each architectural component and their synergistic interaction.

title: Single-cell multi-view clustering based on dual contrastive learning and cross-attention fusion
abstract: Multi-view clustering is a widely utilized technique in single-cell research, with the objective of revealing cellular heterogeneity. However, the scarcity of single-cell data and the difficulty of balancing heterogeneity and similarity in multi-view fusion are still significant issues. We propose scDCCA, a novel single-cell multi-view clustering framework that uniquely integrates three core innovations to address data sparsity and the heterogeneity-similarity trade-off in multi-view fusion. First, it employs a distribution-adaptive variational autoencoder to impute missing values while preserving true biological zeros. Second, it introduces a dual contrastive learning module has been developed to maximize inter-view mutual information in order to extract discriminative features. In addition, a cross-attention mechanism has been incorporated to dynamically fuse features via weighted averaging. Leiden clustering is utilized for the purpose of partitioning. The efficacy of scDCCA in clustering tasks has been demonstrated by evaluations on five datasets.

title: A quantum-assisted federated learning framework for physics-regulated wind speed forecasting under extreme weather conditions
abstract: The increasing frequency of extreme weather events, such as typhoons, necessitates highly accurate and localized forecasting models for power grid stability. While Federated Learning (FL) enables collaborative model training across decentralized weather stations without compromising raw data privacy, standard FL approaches are highly vulnerable to negative transfer, spatial data redundancy, and the catastrophic forgetting of localized physical topologies. To resolve these challenges, this study proposes a novel quantum-assisted federated architecture for region-specific extreme weather forecasting. First, a local Physics-Regulated Neural Network is introduced, embedding Navier–Stokes fluid dynamics directly into the learning objective to ensure physical consistency during anomalous, non-linear typhoon landfalls. Second, a hardware-efficient QAOA is integrated to orchestrate the federated network. Utilizing a Hamming-weight preserving \mathit{XY}$\mathit{XY}$-Mixer, this quantum routing mechanism successfully escapes the local combinatorial minima that trap classical metaheuristics, autonomously selecting an optimal, physically non-redundant subset of client stations. Finally, a target-centric correlation-based fusion strategy aggregates these quantum-selected clients, preserving the unique topological features of the target site. Empirical evaluations utilizing multi-national historical typhoon telemetry demonstrate that the proposed framework decisively outperforms localized models, standard federated networks, and state-of-the-art centralized architectures. The framework achieves a peak variance explanation ({R}^{2}${R}^{2}$) of 0.9568 and a 12.64% reduction in Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) relative to the local baseline. The architecture yields a 10.54% RMSE reduction compared to the strongest classical forecasting baseline, validating the necessity and efficacy of combining physical partial differential equation constraints with quantum combinatorial optimization to maximize the resilience of decentralized meteorological networks.

title: Encoding economic rationality in AI-generated architectural configurations: a knowledge-driven decision support framework
abstract: Generative artificial intelligence is increasingly used in architectural design, yet how such systems relate to economic rationality in spatial configuration remains insufficiently understood. This study proposes a knowledge-driven decision framework to examine whether prompt-defined economic logics are reflected in AI-generated architectural configurations. Using a controlled experimental design, a single generative model produced forty floor plans under identical programmatic constraints while varying the embedded economic logic: cost minimization, value maximization, risk aversion, and balanced strategies. The resulting layouts were analysed through a structured evaluation pipeline combining morphological indicators, space syntax metrics, and daylight-related spatial proxies. These indicators were integrated within a multi-criteria decision-making model to compute an Economic Rationality Score (ERS), which serves as an interpretive measure of alignment between spatial configuration and predefined economic priorities. The results indicate partial and indicator-specific differentiation across economic conditions, with the strongest variation observed in configurational measures such as global integration. Rather than converging toward a single optimal configuration, the model produces structured spatial variation in compactness, circulation organization, hierarchy, and environmental exposure under different prompt conditions. The findings suggest that AI-generated architectural layouts can be interpreted as design outputs exhibiting consistent spatial patterns aligned with prompt-defined economic logics, without implying explicit economic reasoning within the model. The proposed framework contributes to engineering informatics by providing a reproducible approach for analysing and evaluating economically interpretable patterns in AI-assisted architectural design.

title: Predicting antimicrobial peptide properties using enhanced quantum recurrent neural network with self-attention and peephole mechanisms
abstract: Accurate prediction of antimicrobial peptides (AMP) properties is critical for accelerating the design of novel therapeutic agents. In this study, we propose AttPeep-QLSTM, a hybrid quantum-classical sequential learning framework that integrates a quantum self-attention mechanism with a peephole-enhanced quantum LSTM architecture. This design enhances the model’s ability to capture global dependencies while enabling fine-grained temporal control over sequential data. We evaluate the framework on both classification and regression tasks for AMP activity prediction. Experimental results show that AttPeep-QLSTM attains near state-of-the-art predictive performance while requiring orders of magnitude fewer trainable parameters—only 192 compared to the millions used by conventional deep learning baselines—underscoring its efficiency and scalability. Moreover, the model maintains robust predictive capability under quantum noise, suggesting its potential feasibility on near-term noisy intermediate-scale quantum devices. This work highlights the advantages of integrating quantum neural components with classical architectures in bioinformatics, paving the way for future exploration of quantum-enhanced peptide design and sequence modeling.

title: DualNet: A weight-coupled neural network framework for stable physics-informed learning with order reduction
abstract: Recovering primitive functions from derivative data is a classical inverse problem in scientific computing. When embedded into Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) for solving partial differential equations, this operation requires nested automatic differentiation that triggers severe gradient pathologies. Building on the classical mixed and first-order system least-squares formulations and their recent neural-network incarnations (mixed-form and reduced-order PINNs), we propose DualNet, an architectural realization of the mixed/reduced-order idea that enforces the integral–derivative relationship as an exact algebraic identity via weight coupling rather than as a least-squares penalty. DualNet unifies three tasks—function reconstruction from noisy derivatives, potential field recovery from vector fields, and second-order PDE solving via order reduction—within a single architecture. Experiments on Poisson, heat, Burgers, and Helmholtz equations show that DualNet consistently outperforms not only standard PINNs but also recent enhanced variants including FPINNs and CoPINN, while delivering notable training speedup through architectural order reduction, maintaining robustness under extreme data scarcity, and generalizing to non-convex domains without analytical distance functions.

title: Multi-source heterogeneous data-driven interpretable model based on transformer and kolmogorov-arnold networks for streamflow prediction
abstract: Streamflow prediction is vital for water resource management and flood warning. However, the process is highly complex, nonlinear, and uncertain. Traditional data-driven models often struggle to fully integrate multi-source spatiotemporal features and physical mechanisms. To address these challenges, we propose the TKL model, which integrates Transformers, Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks (KAN), and a Local Error Correction (LEC) mechanism. The Transformer’s self-attention mechanism excels at capturing global dependencies and extracting meaningful features. Meanwhile, KAN is adept at handling local continuous variations through learnable activation functions. This combination effectively addresses complex high-dimensional nonlinear regression problems. Additionally, LEC is introduced to refine predictions at local abrupt change points. We utilized 24 types of heterogeneous data, including remote sensing, meteorological factors, and human activity impacts. The model further accounts for spatial correlations between upstream and downstream stations. Validated at nine stations in the Hanjiang River Basin, the TKL model achieved Nash-Sutcliffe Efficiency (NSE) values exceeding 0.96. It consistently outperformed benchmark models in streamflow volume, peak, and lead-time predictions. Finally, interpretable AI methods were employed to reveal the roles of multi-source data and provide physical insights into the hydrological process. The results indicate that the TKL model offers a reliable framework for refined water resource management and accurate flood early warning.

title: SpaMGCL: Neighborhood-aware masked graph contrastive learning for spatial transcriptomics analysis
abstract: The rapid development of spatial transcriptomics (ST) has enabled the simultaneous acquisition of gene expression profiles and spatial coordinates, providing unprecedented opportunities to understand the structural organization of tissues. However, accurate spatial domain identification remains a critical challenge, as existing methods often struggle to capture the complex interactions between gene expression patterns and spatial topology. To address this issue, we propose SpaMGCL (Spatial Masked Graph Contrastive Learning), a novel self-supervised learning framework for spatial domain identification. The proposed framework integrates a masking mechanism with graph contrastive learning, leveraging both gene expression information and spatial constraints to learn highly discriminative latent representations. Specifically, SpaMGCL introduces a masked graph contrastive learning framework to enhance spatial representation learning. First, a masking strategy is employed to simulate missing data, encouraging the model to learn robust representations by reconstructing masked regions. Subsequently, spatial perturbations are applied to generate contrastive views, from which a shared encoder extracts hierarchical features. Meanwhile, contrastive learning is utilized to obtain discriminative spatial representations. Furthermore, SpaMGCL incorporates a neighborhood-aware mechanism that utilizes local spatial context as contrastive anchors, enabling the model to effectively characterize spatially coherent patterns in tissue structures. This design improves intra-domain compactness while enhancing inter-domain separability. We comprehensively evaluate SpaMGCL on seven publicly available ST datasets. Experimental results show that SpaMGCL outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods in spatial domain identification, demonstrating its superior effectiveness and robustness. The implementation is publicly available at https://github.com/wenwenmin/SpaMGCL.

title: TF-SNN: Temporal focus-based dynamic neuron regulation framework for spiking neural networks
abstract: Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) have garnered significant attention in the field of high-performance computing due to their event-driven computational paradigm and strong ability to process spatiotemporal information. However, unlocking their full performance potential critically depends on the appropriate configuration of neuronal dynamics. Prevailing methods generally adopt fixed or uniform parameter strategies across layers or time, which ignore the inherent temporal information heterogeneity among samples and thus lead to significant performance limitations. To address this challenge, we propose an input-adaptive dynamic neuron control framework. Specifically, we introduce a novel sample-level metric, Temporal Focus (TF), which quantifies the concentration of temporal information in each sample through an attention mechanism, providing neurons with a dynamic and input-specific control signal. Furthermore, this TF metric is used as a unified control signal to jointly optimize the neuron firing threshold and surrogate gradient (SG) width, thereby adapting to the varying information densities of different samples and ensuring stable and efficient gradient propagation under different input conditions. Extensive experimental results demonstrate that our approach shows significant improvements on both static and dynamic datasets, particularly on the challenging CIFAR10-DVS dataset, where we achieve an impressive accuracy of 86.7%. This work presents a novel paradigm for the design of low-power SNNs.

title: A decoupled physics-informed expert system for stochastic trajectory prediction via spatio-temporal-frequency fusion
abstract: The modeling and prediction of complex dynamical systems underpin a wide range of engineering applications, including aerospace guidance, autonomous navigation, and robotics. However, practitioners face a persistent cybernetic dilemma: reconciling deterministic physical knowledge with perturbed trajectories and measurements contaminated by multi-scale, non-Gaussian sensor noise and environmental disturbances. To address these gaps, we propose a decoupled physics-informed expert system centered on architectural separation and hierarchical fusion. The proposed framework structurally separates deterministic physical trajectory generation from stochastic deviation modeling. Specifically, a Physics-Informed Trajectory Generation Network (PITGN) establishes a physically consistent baseline trajectory using a velocity-level PINN constraint, while a Stochastic Time-Frequency Dynamics Network (STFD-Net) models the deviation needed to map the baseline trajectory to the disturbed trajectory by integrating a Learnable Spectral Wavelet Attention (LSWA) mechanism with a Neural SDE decoder. Extensive experiments on a high-fidelity 7-DOF aviation dataset demonstrate that our system achieves a mean absolute error of 5.05 m, significantly outperforming traditional filters and standard deep learning baselines. With an inference latency of 25 ms, this modular architecture demonstrates potential for practical deployment, and provides a structured framework for real-time trajectory prediction under uncertain navigation conditions.

title: A hierarchical reinforcement learning approach to personalized decision-making for brain connectivity segmentation
abstract: The automation of empirical decision-making in complex biological signals is a prerequisite for the development of autonomous expert systems that eliminate human-induced bias and promote consistent and reproducible segmentation across subjects. In Major Depressive Disorder (MDD) diagnostics using dynamic functional connectivity (dFC), a parameter-selection bottleneck occurs when fixed temporal scales fail to capture the high inter-subject variability and non-stationary nature of neural dynamics. To resolve this, we propose a domain–algorithm co-design that instantiates Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning (HRL) for personalized dFC segmentation, translating the clinical phenomena of temporal rigidity and transient connectivity transitions into a two-level decision architecture. The macro-agent selects window sizes that match each subject’s characteristic state dwell-time, while the micro-agent selects step ratios that control the sampling density of transient state transitions, decomposing the combinatorially explosive joint (window  ×  step) action space into a tractable coordinated hierarchy. Three clinically constrained design decisions collectively adapt the generic h-DQN to the dFC setting: an asymmetric reward that penalizes false positives more severely than false negatives to avoid MDD over-diagnosis, a ratio-based step parameterization that enforces scale invariance across acquisition protocols, and an asymmetric credit-assignment structure that aligns window-level strategic decisions with step-level tactical refinements. Validated on multi-site MDD datasets across three backbone classifiers, the framework consistently outperforms fixed-parameter and flat RL baselines: F1 improves by up to 5.56 percentage points over the best fixed-parameter baseline within site, by up to 3.2 percentage points in cross-site generalization (Site20 →  Site1/21), and by approximately 9 percentage points over flat RL variants. The framework further generalizes to independent cohorts, yielding +4.04 and +4.61 F1 gains on ABIDE I (ASD) and ADNI (MCI), respectively, and the learned policy transfers to independently trained classifiers with a +3.19 F1 gain over fixed-parameter baselines, indicating that the policy captures subject-adaptive temporal structure rather than classifier-specific inductive biases. Furthermore, the learned policies uncover distinct segmentation regimes in MDD patients that reflect temporal rigidity and reveal a transient sparse-connectivity state (State 5) preferentially occupied by healthy controls, providing explainable biomarkers without a priori hypotheses. These results demonstrate that the framework serves as a principled expert system for subject-adaptive segmentation and as a scalable template for personalized, adaptive time-series analysis in precision psychiatry.

title: AI-enabled virtual immunohistochemistry for real-time molecular inference during intraoperative diagnosis
abstract: Rapid intraoperative diagnosis is vital for guiding surgical decisions in patients with pulmonary nodules, yet current frozen-section evaluation lacks molecular information critical for reliable differentiation of benign and malignant lesions. Conventional immunohistochemistry (IHC), though indispensable for tumor subtyping, is too time-consuming to be applied during surgery. Here, we introduce an AI-enabled virtual IHC framework that reproduces molecular staining directly from hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) slides within the intraoperative diagnostic window. Our multi-task learning model integrates cross-stain registration with weak molecular guidance to capture both morphological and molecular cues, producing virtual IHC slides that are visually and diagnostically indistinguishable from real staining. In blinded tests across diverse lung tissue types, pathologists rated the virtual slides as diagnostically equivalent to authentic IHC, and the entire workflow was completed within 30 min—well within the surgical time limit. This clinically compatible approach seamlessly integrates real-time molecular pathology into the surgical workflow, providing a scalable model for rapid cross-tumor diagnostics and biomarker-specific virtual staining.

title: SF-CFNet: Spatial-frequency collaborative fusion detection network for AI-generated satellite images
abstract: With the rapid progress of generative models, such as generative adversarial networks (GANs) and diffusion models, it has become feasible to readily synthesize forged satellite images with high visual fidelity. This development presents substantial challenges to the existing forgery detection methods for satellite images. Furthermore, most current satellite image detection models are plagued by inherent limitations, including a lack of sufficient ability to capture high-frequency forgery cues, inadequate integration of multi-spectral features, and weak generalization performance under complex scenes and cross-domain data distributions. To address these challenges, a novel Spatial-Frequency Collaborative Fusion Network (SF-CFNet) is put forward for the detection of AI-generated satellite images. Specifically, a frequency-specific dual-attention (FDA) mechanism is devised to enhance the discrimination of crucial forgery-related features. Meanwhile, an adaptive multi-scale feature fusion module integrates hierarchical information across diverse scales. Additionally, a DCT-guided dynamic threshold strategy is incorporated to enhance the robustness of forgery detection under different satellite image qualities. Extensive experiments are conducted on a self-constructed SMTD dataset containing 20,000 samples, including 10,000 forged satellite images generated by GANs and diffusion models, as well as the public DeepFake_GeoSat dataset. Experimental results demonstrate that SF-CFNet consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods under the main validated experimental setting, achieving an accuracy of 98.95%, precision of 99.75%, recall of 98.17%, and an F1-score of 98.96%.

title: HGP-Det: A lightweight reinforcement learning framework for efficient object detection
abstract: Existing deep reinforcement learning-based object detection methods suffer from three critical limitations: sample clustering destabilises policy learning, static reward functions fail to balance localisation accuracy with exploration efficiency, and hyperparameter sensitivity impedes model convergence. To address these challenges, we propose HGP-Det, a lightweight reinforcement learning framework comprising three core innovations. First, the Hilbert Geometry-aware Deep Q-Network (HK-DQN) addresses sample clustering via a Hilbert space diversity-aware sampling mechanism and improves Q-value estimation through a geometry-aware network with learnable B-spline activations. Second, the Neural-PDE Reward Function (NPRF) encodes physics-inspired trajectory constraints into a decomposable multi-objective reward signal, guiding the agent to develop a coarse-to-fine localisation strategy. Third, Multi-Agent Game Optimization (MAGO) adaptively searches for optimal learning rates via a Stackelberg game-driven three-agent architecture, accelerating convergence and stabilising training. Experiments on VOC, COCO, and SF datasets demonstrate that HGP-Det achieves 80.3% mAP (VOC), 81.2% mAP (COCO), and 80.6% Precision (SF) at only 1.56 GFLOPs, attaining 91.4% of the detection accuracy of YOLOv11s while requiring merely 7.2% of its computational cost, establishing a favourable accuracy–efficiency trade-off for deployment on resource-constrained edge devices. The source code is publicly available at https://github.com/Lzfsir/HGP-Det.git.

title: DCRL : A dual contrastive representation learning framework for enhanced spatial domain identification in transcriptomics
abstract: Spatial transcriptomics integrates spatial positional information with gene expression profiles, enabling more accurate spatial domain identification. However, existing methods often struggle to balance intra-domain continuity with inter-domain separability, leading to boundaries that are either discontinuous or overly smoothed. To address this issue, we propose DCRL, a dual contrastive representation learning framework for learning discriminative and spatially coherent spot embeddings. DCRL employs two complementary contrastive strategies. First, cross-view contrastive learning enhances the correspondence between spatial and gene-expression embeddings of the same spot, thereby improving view consistency. Second, instance-level contrastive learning, guided by dynamic pseudo-labels, promotes intra-domain compactness and inter-domain separability. Together, these components improve domain coherence and boundary clarity. We evaluate DCRL on multiple public spatial transcriptomics datasets and show that it achieves strong overall performance in spatial domain identification compared with state-of-the-art methods.

title: PDGAGRN: Graph diffusion pretraining and dynamic graph learning for gene regulatory network inference from single-cell RNA-sequencing data
abstract: Gene regulatory networks (GRNs) are crucial for revealing complex life activities and disease mechanisms. However, GRN inference tasks frequently face challenges involving the high-dimensional sparsity and high false-positive rates of single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) data. Existing methods often rely heavily on sparse static prior knowledge and single graph convolution paradigms, struggling to effectively capture global topological structures and nonlinear long-range dependencies. This restricts inference accuracy and reliability in sparse data. To address this, this paper proposes PDGAGRN, a method based on graph diffusion pre-training, dynamic graph learning, and hierarchical adaptive fusion. First, through self-supervised graph diffusion pre-training, the model learns global topological structures and long-range dependencies. This mitigates perception limitations of graph convolution paradigms in sparse data, enabling the capture of comprehensive regulatory information. Additionally, dynamic graph learning expands static priors by mining potential regulatory relationships, enriching sparse priors to effectively learn complex nonlinear regulatory relationships in sparse data. Finally, hierarchical feature fusion and role-aware transformations adaptively integrate multi-scale features, further improving GRN inference precision on sparse data. Comprehensive evaluations on extensive datasets covering diverse cell types and ground-truth networks demonstrate that PDGAGRN significantly surpasses state-of-the-art (SOTA) methods, particularly leading by a large margin in the sparsity-sensitive AUPRC metric. These results confirm PDGAGRN’s effectiveness in alleviating high-dimensional sparsity impacts and reducing false-positive rates. Furthermore, in a case study of human mature hepatocytes, the model exhibits high precision and successfully predicts multiple potential novel regulatory relationships with high confidence, indicating PDGAGRN’s significant potential in GRN inference.

title: Nexus: Neuro-guided expert-routed pre-training for brain representation learning from sMRI
abstract: Brain representation learning from structural Magnetic Resonance Imaging (sMRI) via pre-training has emerged as a powerful paradigm for computer-aided neurological analysis. However, prevailing general pre-training methods often treat the brain as a generic 3D object, relying solely on anatomical appearance without integrating complex intrinsic neurobiological traits. To address this, we propose Nexus (Neuro-guided expert-routed pre-training for sMRI) as a novel framework embedding comprehensive neurobiological priors and demographic metadata into a unified encoder. We design diverse pre-training objectives that simultaneously capture macroscopic morphology, developmental trajectories, and structure-function associations. This compels the model to learn the intrinsic coupling between anatomical structures and neurobiological properties. To manage these objectives and resolve inherent gradient conflicts, we deploy a task-adaptive mixture of experts architecture regularized by orthogonality constraints. This adaptively allocates specialized experts to distinct targets, ensuring efficient computation and preventing task interference. Additionally, we introduce a Structure-Aware Local Shuffle (SA-LS) strategy that selectively preserves essential anatomical boundaries while perturbing local textures, generating challenging, neurobiologically meaningful inputs that compel the model to perform profound geometric reasoning. Extensive experiments demonstrate that Nexus achieves state-of-the-art performance in diverse disease diagnosis tasks, significantly outperforming existing general and neuro-guided pre-training baselines. Rigorous analyses of phenotype prediction and reliability validate the neurobiological plausibility and robustness of the learned representations. Finally, the expert routing mechanism’s interpretability reveals neurobiologically consistent correlations between pre-training objectives and clinical targets, establishing a transparent foundation for clinical decision support.

title: SDDCA: State-driven discrete diffusion model with cohesive attention embedding for change detection of remote sensing image
abstract: Change detection (CD) is a critical interpretive application in remote sensing (RS) that aims to investigate variations in land cover from bi-temporal RS images, and serves in the fields of environmental monitoring and urban planning. Current CNN-based CD methods struggle to capture global features, leading to insufficient detail detection in change regions. While the long-range dependencies of Transformer-based and Mamba-based models aid in detail expression, they still have shortcomings in effectively detecting false changes. Alternatively, with the iterative generation and multi-step reasoning processes, diffusion-model-based CD methods exhibit strength by progressively refining discrepancies between bi-temporal RS images. In this paper, we propose a novel discrete diffusion-based CD paradigm and establish a state-driven discrete diffusion model with cohesive attention embedding (SDDCA) for change region generation. Due to the inherent characteristics of the CD task, we particularly define the two discrete states denoted as changed and unchanged to reflect the variations in the transition matrices within the SDDCA model. Notably, existing diffusion-model-based CD methods count on the addition and estimation of Gaussian noise to realize the diffusion process, which involves enormous diffusion iteration steps and model parameters. By contrast, with the presented binary diffusion pattern, the proposed model facilitates the generation of high-quality change masks and offers greater efficiency than traditional diffusion-model-based CD methods. Furthermore, we present the cohesive attention embedding (CAE) module that seamlessly integrates discrepancy features into the discrete diffusion process through a hybrid cross-attention mechanism. Additionally, the presented multi-domain discrepancy (MDD) module and the pyramid hierarchical fusion (PHF) module acquire and concatenate frequency information with spatial features for the CAE module. Comprehensive experiments on three publicly accessible CD datasets demonstrate that the proposed SDDCA outperforms other state-of-the-art (SOTA) methods, and achieves an F1-score of 91.24%, 92.96%, and 87.20% on LEVIR-CD, WHU-CD, and GZ-CD, respectively.

title: Semantic-aware pruning of large language models via neuron importance explanation
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have become essential for knowledge-intensive applications, ranging from enterprise knowledge management to clinical and legal decision support. However, their extensive parameterization creates substantial computational and memory requirements that hinder practical deployment in resource-constrained environments such as edge devices and enterprise systems with limited infrastructure. While structured pruning shows promise for LLM compression, existing methods apply static masks that cannot adapt to diverse input characteristics, resulting in inconsistent performance across different application domains and task distributions. In this work, we present SeAP, a semantic-aware dynamic structured pruning framework designed for efficient deployment of intelligent language systems. Our framework enables adaptive model compression through two key components: (1) an explainability-guided importance estimation method that discovers diverse representative pruning patterns by fusing local and global neuron importance from calibration data, and (2) a lightweight router module that efficiently assigns optimal compression strategies for each input at the pre-fill stage. The pipeline keeps the LLM backbone frozen and requires only a small calibration set, allowing it to be retrofitted into existing expert-system deployments. Extensive experimental results on LLaMA-2/3, Qwen2, and Phi-2 demonstrate that SeAP outperforms state-of-the-art structured pruning methods across diverse language modeling and commonsense reasoning tasks, achieving competitive performance with reductions in memory and inference latency, highlighting its potential for real-world expert-system deployment.

title: Single-shot fringe projection profilometry with a TGV-regularized u-net enhanced fourier neural operator
abstract: Balancing reconstruction speed and accuracy remains a significant challenge in Fringe Projection Profilometry (FPP). While single-shot structured light illumination techniques exhibit superior performance in real-time scanning, they often suffer from compromised reconstruction quality, particularly on surfaces with sharp discontinuities. To address this limitation, we propose a reconstruction scheme based on a U-Net enhanced Fourier Neural Operator (U-FNO) regularized by Total Generalized Variation (TGV). This framework synergistically combines a second-order TGV model with the U-FNO architecture. Specifically, a dual-frequency composite fringe pattern is generated via a multi-frequency modulation strategy. Subsequently, the U-FNO model is employed to accurately demodulate the designed frequency components from the single captured frame. The absolute phase is then recovered through a frequency mixing strategy, enabling the final 3D shape reconstruction. Experiments conducted on challenging scenarios, including orthogonal and multi-frequency co-directional composite fringe patterns, demonstrate that the proposed method generates significantly more accurate 3D point clouds for surfaces with discontinuities, rapid depth changes, and complex textures when compared to conventional and representative approaches. The method achieves a single-shot reconstruction precision ranging from 24.9 μm to 71.2 μm depending on the surface texture.

title: Novel physics-informed spatiotemporal gated long short-term memory fault prediction for permanent magnet synchronous motor compressors in cold chain logistics
abstract: This paper proposes a Physics-Informed Spatiotemporal Gated Long Short-Term Memory (PI-STG-LSTM) network for fault propagation modeling and intelligent diagnosis of the inverter compressor of a permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM) used in cold chain logistics trucks, addressing bearing wear, rotor eccentricity, and refrigerant leakage across coupled electromechanical and thermal systems. Unlike existing spatiotemporal gated hybrids that combine spatial gating, recurrence, and attention in a purely data-driven manner, such as the spatial–temporal gated hybrid Transformer network (STGHTN) and the graph-attention recurrent network (GAttenRNN), the proposed framework is distinguished by three physics-informed algorithmic mechanisms rather than by the assembly of existing blocks. The spatial gating weights are not freely learned but are analytically derived from and constrained by first-principles coupling equations, namely Archard’s wear law, rotor eccentricity dynamics, and the thermodynamic refrigerant-leakage relation, so that feature propagation is forced to follow physically admissible trajectories. A strictly causal, anti-reverse-time spatiotemporal influence matrix encodes the directional fault-propagation chain from bearing wear to rotor eccentricity to refrigerant leakage to compressor-load rise, eliminating the spurious bidirectional associations that data-driven graphs are prone to learn. A physics-consistency regularization term penalizes any deviation of the learned cross-node propagation from the prescribed physical chain, providing an explicit inductive bias that pure attention models lack. A cross-node forgetting control suppresses non-adjacent noise and a sliding-window normalization module adapts to startup, steady-state, and load-switching phases. Experiments combining fast Fourier transform (FFT) spectral screening, hybrid LSTM–Transformer prediction, and receiver operating characteristic–area under curve (ROC-AUC) evaluation, together with a controlled architectural ablation and direct benchmarking against CNN-LSTM, Attention-Bi-LSTM, GCN-LSTM, GAT-LSTM, Transformer-TCN, STGHTN, and GAttenRNN, confirm that PI-STG-LSTM attains superior fault detection, prediction, and robustness, thereby improving reliability and energy efficiency in cold chain logistics systems.

title: Task-aware text prompt fusion with contrastive learning for zero-shot anomaly detection
abstract: Recently, vision-language pre-trained models, such as CLIP, have demonstrated significant potential in zero-shot anomaly detection. Current research primarily focuses on adapting CLIP for anomaly detection through either prompt learning or adapter. However, the original CLIP encoder produces anomaly-unawareness features due to pretraining on generic image-text pairs and lacking explicit guidance for anomaly detection tasks. To address this limitation, we introduce task-specific supervisory signals into the feature learning process. The insight is to leverage normal text prompts to enhance normal information in images while suppressing anomalous, whereas anomalous text prompts are designed to amplify abnormal features and diminish normal signals. Compared to directly extracting image features from a frozen visual encoder, such task-aware text-prompted image features are more adaptive to anomaly detection, thereby facilitating more effective prompt learning. Specifically, we first design a task-aware text prompt fusion module to generate image features embedded with text prompts. Then, we introduce contrastive learning that explicitly regulates the distance between image features fused with normal text prompts and those fused with anomalous text prompts. Finally, we design a diversity loss function for prompt ensemble strategy. Extensive experiments on multiple industrial and medical datasets demonstrate that the proposed method achieves improved performance in zero-shot anomaly detection. The code is available at https://github.com/lilianoa/MFAD-CLIP.

title: Modeling time-frequency deep learning to estimate excessive groundwater extraction induced land subsidence along Taiwan high-speed rail corridors
abstract: Land subsidence is a critical geohazard in regions where intensive groundwater extraction coincides with major infrastructure corridors. Globally, areas in the United States, China, and Indonesia have reported subsidence rates of several centimeters per year, threatening transportation networks and increasing maintenance costs. In Taiwan, the problem is particularly pronounced in Chiayi County, where agricultural irrigation and industrial water demands have historically driven excessive groundwater withdrawal. This has caused severe land subsidence along the High-Speed Railway (HSR) rail track, posing a significant threat to operational safety. Traditional monitoring techniques, such as leveling surveys and InSAR-based remote sensing, provide valuable measurements but lack predictive capabilities for proactive risk management. To address this challenge, this study proposes a novel optimized deep learning model, the Artificial Satellite Search Algorithm-Revolving Gate Fourier Transformation (ASSA-RGFT). The model integrates two key mechanisms: first, it predicts groundwater levels; second, these predictions are used as input variables for forecasting land subsidence. In the comparative experiments conducted with other advanced AI models, the proposed ASSA-RGFT achieved the highest RI values of 0.968 and 0.953 on the testing set, respectively, for Phase 1 (groundwater level) and Phase 2 (land subsidence), outperforming all benchmark models across all evaluation metrics. Given its strong predictive performance, the ASSA-RGFT model offers an effective decision-support tool for implementing timely and targeted land subsidence mitigation strategies, enhancing the long-term safety and reliability of high-speed rail operations.

title: What the doodle: Sketching mental pictures with decoding brain signals, language understanding, and AI creativity
abstract: Decoding and visualizing mental imagery from brain activity remains a significant challenge at the intersection of neuroscience and artificial intelligence. While recent advancements in neural decoding have enabled the reconstruction of perceived stimuli, translating abstract and subjective mental representations into accurate visual depictions is still an open problem due to the inherent noise and variability in neuroimaging data. To address this, we propose NeuroCanvas, a novel framework that bridges the gap between electroencephalography (EEG) based brain decoding and visual concept generation through a multi-stage approach. Our method first employs deep learning models to map EEG signals into initial textual descriptions, providing a preliminary representation of the imagined content. These descriptions are then refined using large language models (LLMs) to enhance their semantic coherence and contextual richness while mitigating the impact of neural noise and inter-subject variability. The optimized text embeddings serve as input to a generative autoregressive network, which synthesizes high-fidelity images closely aligned with the original mental pictures. We evaluate the effectiveness of NeuroCanvas through extensive experiments, demonstrating significant improvements in semantic alignment, visual quality, and cross-subject generalization compared to direct EEG-to-image mapping baselines. Furthermore, the intermediate textual representations provide an inherently inspectable layer within the pipeline, offering the potential for iterative user refinement of generated visualisations, pending formal usability. Our framework achieves a Semantic Fidelity Score of 0.593 on the EEG-Image dataset, representing a 74% improvement over direct traditional methods (0.341) and maintains robust performance with Neuro-Visual Coherence scores above 0.487 across all datasets while achieving Cross-Subject Generalization errors below 0.281. Our work has potential applications in fields such as creative design, psychotherapy, and neuroscientific research, providing a tool for investigating the neural basis of visual imagination.

title: MSMCNN-CL : A multi-scale and multi-conformation neural network with scaffold-guided contrastive learning for molecular property prediction
abstract: Molecular property prediction is a fundamental task in drug discovery. However, existing methods often rely on single-scale features and the single molecular conformation. These limitations hinder their ability to model conformation-sensitive properties and long-range interactions, thereby limiting the predictive performance. To address these challenges, we propose a multi-scale and multi-conformation fusion graph neural network with scaffold-guided contrastive learning for molecular property prediction. We design a multi-scale graph neural network as the backbone that performs hierarchical feature extraction by enabling message passing at both atomic and fragment levels. A multi-conformation feature enhancement module is developed, which combines the universal three-dimensional molecular representation learning framework with a Transformer encoder to extract rich conformation-aware features. These features are fused with multi-scale representations through a cross-attention mechanism, followed by the gating layer and the multilayer perceptron for property prediction. To further improve generalization, we design a scaffold-guided contrastive learning strategy that regularizes the molecular representation space. Extensive experiments on seven datasets from the benchmark for molecular machine learning demonstrate that our model consistently outperforms baselines, achieving an average error reduction of 0.12 in regression tasks and a 2.6% performance gain in classification tasks. To evaluate real-world applicability, we further conduct experiments on thirteen datasets covering molecular absorption, distribution, metabolism, excretion, and toxicity properties, where our model also presents competitive results. Furthermore, performance analysis results demonstrates the effective and robustness of our model and ablation experiments demonstrate that each component contributes to overall performance.

title: Artificial intelligence-based beam configuration inference with received power-only sensing feedback for beamforming wireless power transfer
abstract: Efficient beam acquisition is a critical challenge in beamforming wireless power transfer (WPT) systems because the phase configuration that maximizes the received power is typically obtained through repeated beam probing or exhaustive codebook sweeping. Although such approaches provide reliable beam selection, they incur substantial latency and energy overhead, particularly when high-resolution phase control is required. This work presents an artificial intelligence-based beam configuration inference framework for beamforming WPT under a received power-only sensing feedback setting. Instead of explicitly estimating receiver coordinates, the proposed method directly infers a fine-grained 6-bit phase-index map from a coarse 4-bit received-power fingerprint acquired during beam scanning. The framework uses only scalar WPT received-power measurements obtained from the receiver-side power sensor and does not require channel state information (CSI), communication-link received signal strength indicator (RSSI), or multiple radio-frequency (RF) chains. A compact residual convolutional neural network is trained using labels generated by brute-force codebook sweeping, which is used only as an offline reference and upper-bound baseline. To support embedded deployment, quantization-aware implementation is adopted, and low-bit inference characteristics are investigated using fake quantization and additive-power-of-two quantization. Hardware measurements on a 5.8-GHz 8  ×  8 phased-array WPT platform demonstrate that the proposed method achieves received-power performance comparable to that of full 6-bit brute-force sweeping while reducing beam-acquisition time by 3.9 ×  and reducing the measured beam-control hardware dynamic power by approximately 8%, including neural-network inference overhead. These results show that intelligent phase-map inference from received power-only sensing feedback is an effective strategy for practical low-complexity WPT beam control.

title: Physics-informed adaptive multi-head attention LSTM for shape prediction of variable curvature/torsion spatial tubes in free bending forming
abstract: Dynamically coupled multi-parameter systems with stringent physical constraints are ubiquitous in advanced manufacturing processes. Taking the free bending forming of variable curvature/torsion spatial tubes as an example, high-precision prediction of their forming states faces three fundamental challenges: capturing cross-parameter coupling effects, modeling complex temporal dependencies, and enforcing physical consistency. To address these issues, this paper proposes a physics-informed adaptive multi-head attention LSTM (PAMA-LSTM) framework for temporal prediction, which establishes a closed-loop architecture integrating coupling capture, feature fusion, physical constraints, and performance optimization. A customized multi-head attention mechanism adaptively captures dynamic coupling patterns. A cross-head fusion layer integrates features and quantifies the contribution of each attention head to reduce redundancy. A physics-informed loss function integrates multi-head attention weights with physical constraints as penalty terms to ensure prediction rationality. A Bayesian strategy optimizes hyperparameters to maximize overall performance. Meanwhile, the model leverages LSTM units to capture the dynamic temporal evolution of the forming process, accurately reflecting the influence of historical states on the current state. Experimental results on free bending forming demonstrate that PAMA-LSTM significantly outperforms baseline and ablation models in curvature/torsion prediction and axis reconstruction. PAMA-LSTM offers a systematic approach to integrating process mechanisms with deep learning in complex forming domains, achieving an engineering balance among accuracy, robustness, and physical consistency. It holds significant implications for intelligent manufacturing and real-time process optimization.

title: Conditional disentangled information bottleneck for multi-view molecular graph representation learning
abstract: Molecular representation learning is fundamental to drug discovery and materials design. Graph neural networks have demonstrated strong capabilities for modeling molecular graphs, yet most methods rely solely on 2D topology and underutilize 3D geometric information crucial for many properties. Recent multi-view methods integrate 2D and 3D views through cross-view alignment. However, these methods typically assume strong alignment between views and focus on extracting shared semantics, which may introduce redundant information or suppress informative view-specific signals, limiting downstream performance. In this work, we propose the Conditional Disentangled Information Bottleneck (CDIB), a principled information-theoretic framework for multi-view molecular representation learning. CDIB introduces a novel conditional disentangled information bottleneck objective that preserves predictive sufficiency while promoting compact and complementary latent representations across 2D and 3D views. Specifically, CDIB decomposes multi-view embeddings into a view-common representation that captures predictive information shared across views, and view-specific representations that preserve complementary structural or geometric cues. We derive a tractable optimization bound that provides a theoretical foundation for the implementation of CDIB within a unified framework. Extensive experiments on ten MoleculeNet benchmarks show that CDIB achieves state-of-the-art performance on seven datasets. In particular, CDIB reduces root mean squared error (RMSE) by an average of 7.5% on regression benchmarks and achieves up to a 1.3 ROC-AUC point improvement on classification benchmarks. Representation analyses demonstrate that CDIB effectively separates view-common and view-specific information, yielding molecular representations with clearer chemical semantics and improved interpretability.

title: A trustworthy deep learning framework for urban climate downscaling via physics-informed diffusion and topology-aware graph neural operators
abstract:
Urban areas face an escalating climate crisis, yet the resolution gap between coarse atmospheric reanalysis data operating at approximately 30-kilometer grid spacing and the kilometer-scale predictions required for urban planning remains a critical challenge. While deep learning methods achieve high accuracy in climate prediction tasks, they typically fail to satisfy three essential properties for operational deployment: adherence to physical conservation laws, stable predictions under input perturbations, and generalizability to new urban environments without retraining. This paper introduces a two-stage framework that defines and achieves trustworthy urban climate inference, where trustworthiness encompasses physical consistency, prediction stability, and cross-city generalizability.

In the first stage, a Stochastic Physics-Informed Diffusion Model (SPIDM) corrects systematic biases in coarse climate data while simultaneously quantifying predictive uncertainty through a stochastic differential equation framework. In the second stage, a Deep Graph Fourier Neural Operator (DeepGFNO) performs coarse-to-fine urban climate inference on a novel hybrid graph structure that jointly encodes geographic proximity and land-use similarity derived from satellite-based vegetation indices.

Validated on reanalysis climate data for two Egyptian cities with distinct climatic profiles, the framework achieves: (1) a 54% reduction in wind field divergence error, confirming adherence to mass conservation; (2) a 27% improvement in prediction stability relative to a standard convolutional neural network baseline; (3) 27% better zero-shot transfer performance to an entirely unseen city; and (4) a 62% reduction in prediction error through hybrid graph design relative to geographic-only graph structures. Although a standard encoder-decoder network achieves marginally better in-domain accuracy, it suffers 257% performance degradation when transferred to a new city, confirming that it memorizes location-specific spatial patterns rather than learning transferable physical principles. By prioritizing trustworthiness criteria and providing a complete open-source implementation with illustrative urban planning applications, this work establishes a deployment-oriented framework in which zero-shot transfer quantifies transferable physical knowledge across the tested arid and Mediterranean regimes and brief few-shot adaptation (50 target-city samples) provides the operational accuracy required for fine-grained urban planning. Broader validation across diverse climatic regimes is identified as an important direction for future research.
